question: Which of the following pregnancy-related dermatoses is least likely to recur in subsequent pregnancies?

choices.A: Pruritic urticaria! papules and plaques of pregnancy (PUPP)

correct_text: Pruritic urticaria! papules and plaques of pregnancy (PUPP)
explanation: PUPP which is also called polymorphic eruption of pregnancy occurs in the first pregnancy and seldom recurs in subsequent pregnancies. Both pemphigoid gestationis and intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy can recur with subsequent pregnancies or with the use of oral contraceptives. Atopic eruption of pregnancy can be the first manifestation of atopic disease in a susceptible person.

question: A colleague has performed a biopsy for a blistering condition and you receive the histology report stating that there is a subepidermal blister with a dense neutrophilic infiltrate; no eosinophils are seen. Direct immunofluoresence is not available. Which of the following disorders is most likely to show this histological appearance?
explanation: The type of cell infiltrate together with the direct immunofluoresence can be very helpful in establishing a histological differential. Subepidermal bullae with a predominantly neutrophilic infiltrate include: linear lgA disease, dermatitis herpetiformis, mucous membrane pemphigoid, bullous lupus erythematosus and Sweet s syndrome. Bullous mastocytosis has subepidermal bullae with mast cells. Bullous pemphigoid has a predominantly eosinophilic infiltrate although a neutrophilic infiltrate may occur. Erythema multiforme has a predominantly lymphocytic infiltrate. Epidermolysis bullosa acquisita typically is cell-poor but some cases may have a neutrophilic infiltrate. 87 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: A 6-week old baby presented with multiple papules, pustules and closed comedones on both cheeks. Examination of the rest of the skin was unremarkable and he was otherwise a healthy neonate. The most likely diagnosis is
explanation: Neonatal acne consists of both inflammatory lesions and comedones. It presents in the first three months of life. This occurs due to the presence of the maternal hormones which stimulate the sebaceous glands In the neonate. The condition resolves spontaneously without treatment in the first three months of life. Neonatal cephalic pustulosis is a pustular condition mainly affecting the head of neonates, without comedones. This is may be due to overgrowth of various Malassezia species. Infantile acne appears after the age of three months and is more common in boys due to higher levels oftestosterone in the first 6-12 months of life. There may be a positive family history, and the condition includes both inflammatory and comedonal lesions, however often inflammatory lesions predominate and in severe cases, cystic acne may occur. Children with infantile acne should be evaluated with an endocrinological screening for underlying abnormalities, and there may be a risk for severe acne later in life. Staphylococcal pustulosis presents with diffuse pustules in the absence of comedones, on the trunk and limbs. 88 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: A 4-year old boy presented with generalized tender macular erythema whkh was most prominent on the skin around his mouth and nose, and in the groin area. Two days after his hospitalization, the erythematous rash started to desquamate, particularly in his groin area. He was feverish a;1d appeared lethargic, but had no mucou~ membrane involvement and no lymphadenopathy. His mother said that he had a sore throat two days prior to his eruption and has not been on any medication. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome is characterized by generalized tender macular erythema which desquamates within few days, particularly on the skin around the mouth, nose and flexural areas. Typically, large superficial flaccid bullae may appear on the background of the erythema and leave painful denuded areas. The child is often lethargic and febrile and the condition is due to staphylococcal exfoliating toxin. Prompt treatment with anti-staphylococcal antibiotics results in full recovery and the prognosis is generally very good. Toxic epidermal necrolysis would certainly be in the differential, however, this condition is often secondary to drugs and occ•Jrs more in adults than children, and often involves the mucous membranes. Diagnostic biopsy is sometimes required to differentiate the two conditions. In toxic epidermal necrolysis, full epidermal necrosis Is seen with minimal dermal infiltrate. The defect (split) in staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome is in the subcorneal layer. Kawasaki s disease may give rise to desquamation in the flexural area; however, the diagnosis requires the presence of high fever lasting for at least five days and four of the following criteria: conjunctiva! injection, mucous membrane changes (particularly strawberry tongue appearance), erythema or oedema of the palms and soles, and cervical lymphadenopathy. question: A 43-year old man presented with a 10-year history of red-brown patches in the axillae with distinct borders and absence of any scaling. The condition was mildly pruritic and scrapings were negative for fungal hypahe or spores. Examination unde, Wood's light showed coral-pink fluorescence. The organism responsible for this condition is
explanation: Erythrasma can be treated with topical or oral erythromycin. Epidermophyton floccosum may affect the axillae, although it is commonly present in the groins. It is a fungus that does not fluoresce; scrapings can be positive for microscopy and culture. Trichophyton verrucosum is a zoophilic dermatophyte found in cattle and usually results in a severe inflammatory dermatomycosis. 89 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: A 24-year old woman presents with excessive facial hair and acne. There is a history of menstrual irregularities as well. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: N Hirsutism is defined as excessive terminal hair growth in women in the androgen-sensitive areas. Polycystic ovarian syndrome is the commonest endocrinological cause for hirsutism. N Diagnosis of polycystic ovarian syndrome requires two out of three of the following: positive imaging, menstrual abnormalities and signs of hyperandrogenism, which can be remembered by the acronym SAHA, that stands for Seborrohea, Acne, Hirsutism and Androgenetic alopecia.

question: A-30 year old, 24-weeks pregnant patient has severe atopic eczema not respondinr, to topical emollients alone. Which of the following drugs is an absolute contra-indication in pregnancy?
explanation: N Although generally systemic treatments should be avoided in pregnancy if possible, all the above, with the exception of mycophenolate mofetil, can be used in pregnancy.

question: Which of the following drugs is most likely to cause drug-induced linear lgA disease?
explanation: Vancomycin is the most common cause of drug induced linear lgA disease. Penicillamine can cause both drug-induced pemphigus and mucous membrane pemphigoid, and long-term use can result in elastosis perforans serpiginosa, in which elastic fibres extrude through the epidermis.

question: A 26-year old man has been troubled with intense burning erythema with swelling on sun exposed sites within minutes of exposure to sunlight. This has been impact ing negatively on his quality of life and he is therefore working and spending most of his time indoors. On further questioning, the erythema and swelling normally subsides within few hours. He has tried various sun avoidance measures and the use of high factor sun creams and is enquiring about systemic treatment. Which of the following systemic treatments is the first line treatment for this condition?
explanation: Although immunosuppressive therapies can certainly be used with some degree of success in patients with solar urticaria, antihistamines remain first choice treatment. UVB desensitisation can also be used in this condition provided that patients do not show sensitivity to that particular wavelength. Erythema and wheals in solar urticaria develop within seconds to minutes following exposure to sunlight and almost always subside within 24 hours. 90 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: Which of the following is not a feature of drug rash (or reaction) with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS) syndrome?
explanation: DRESS is a serious drug eruption that typically presents with an exanthematous eruption with fever, lymphadenopathy, oedema of the face, peripheral eosinophilia, atypical lymphocytes and visceral involvement. ,., Liver and krdney involvement may be seen. The latency period may take anywhere between 1-8 weeks, although this may be much earlier with re-exposure to the drug. A pustular eruption is not a feature of DRESS syndrome and is seen in acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis.

question: What is the inheritance pattern for incontinentia pigmenti?
explanation: Incontinentia pigmenti is a genodermatosis that primarily affects females as males do not survive this X-linked dominant disorder, unless they are mosaic. The commonest mutation involves a deletion in the NEMO gene on the long arm of the X chromosome. The condition has four stages; inflammatory vesicular stage which tends to be along Blaschko s lines, a verrucous stage, hyperpigmented, and finally hypopigmented stage in which whorls and swirls develop in a characteristic Chinese letter pattern. There is associated ectodermal dysplasia and nail changes may occur including onycholysis, onychodystrophy and subungual hyperkeratosis. Systemic defects can occur, and in particular, brain and eye involvement. Patients with incontinentia pigmenti should have neurological and ophthalmic assessment.

question: A 20-year old man presents with acute onset of severe acne associated with malaise, fever and arthralgia. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Acne conglobata is a specific variant of acne characterised by large comedones with multiple openings, predominantly on the face and back. A positive family history is often found and this should not be confused with acne fulminans which is a severe form of acne that tends to affect young males and presents with malaise, fever, arthralgia and liver involvement. Unlike acne conglobata, haemorrhagic crusted ulcerative lesion can be found in acne fulminans. 91 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: A 46-year old patient presents with multiple skin tags and skin-coloured papules on the face and neck. She has previously been admitted on three occasions for spontaneous pneumothoraces. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Birt-Hogg-Dube syndrome manifests as fibrofolliculomas, trichodiscomas and acrochordons. This is an autosomal dominant disorder and can be associated with renal and pulmonary cysts; and can present with pneumothoraces. Rombo syndrome presents with basal cell carcinomas, trichoepitheliomas, hypotrichosis, atrophoderma and telangiectasia. Bazex-Dupre-Christol syndrome presents with basal cell carcinomas, follicular at,ophoderma, pili torti, scrotal tongue, spiny hyperkeratosis, and neuropsychiatt ic symptoms. It is an X-linked dominant disorder. Gorlin s syndrome presents with basal cell carcinomas, palmo-plantar pits, odontogenic jaw cysts, frontal bossing, ovarian carcinoma/ fibroma, medulloblastomas, lipomas, and epidermal cysts. It Is an autosomal dominant disorder due to PTCH1 gene defect.

question: The dermatology registrar in the department excised an atypical looking mole on the shoulder of a 24-year old sun worshipper. Hi5tology showed superficial spreading melanoma with a Breslow thickness of 1.3 mm without ulceration. You are referring the patient to the plastic surgeon for re-excision. What should be the re-excision margins?
explanation: 5 mm is the margin is employed for melanoma in-situ and lentigo maligna (melanoma In situ In sun-damaged skin). The guidelines suggest that in thin melanomas (less than 1 mm in depth), these should be excised with a margin of at least 1 cm and for melanomas, between 1.01-2 mm a margin of 2 cm when possible. 2 mm margin is the initial margin used for atypical naevi as was the case here. 92 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: Which of the following genodermatoses is inherited in an X-linked dominar.t fashion?
explanation: Conradi-Hunermann syndrome is inherited in an X-linked dominant pattern. Patients are often born with a collodion-like membrane followed by an ichthyosiform ervthroderma in Blaschko s lines. There may also be follicular atrophoderma, scarring alopecia, scoliosis and cataracts. Sjogren-Larsson syndrome is an autosomal recessive disorder presents with ichthyosis at birth with spastic paralysis and mental retardation. Netherton s syndrome is an autosomal recessive disorder that presents with an exfoli 3tive 1:?ryt:hroderma with ichthyosis linearis circumflexa; the typical double edged migratory scale. The typir:al feature is the so-called bamboo hairs showing microscopically the typical trichorrhexis invaginata. Lamellar ichthyosis presents with a collodion baby at birth. It is an autosomal recessive disorder. Most patients develop later in life features of ectropion, inverted ears, plate-like scale, which is often dirty brown , and palmo-plantar keratoderma. Xeroderma pigmentosum is an autosomal recessive disorder.

question: Which of the following antibodies is most specific for systemic lupus erythematosus?
explanation: In systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) anti-nuclear antibody is positive in the majority of patients. Immunological abnormalities including the finding of anti-Sm and anti-dsDNA antibodies form one of the criteria for diagnosis of SLE. Anti-Sm antibodies are specific to SLE and are found in around 20-30% of patients. Anti-ds-DNA antibodies are also specific to this condition (also in lupoid hepatitis) and the titres may correlate with both renal involvement and disease activity (unlike the anti-Sm antibody).

question: Which of the following tumours is most likely to develop in organ transplant recipients?
explanation: Although the incidence of cutaneous tumours and dysplastic lesions is greatly increased in patients with organ transplantation due to immune suppression, the risk of squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) in particular is greatly increased (x 60-250) and the usual basal cell carcinoma: sec incidence ratio of 4:1 is reversed. The risk of basal cell carcinoma and melanoma is also Increased but to a lesser degree compared to secs. 93 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: A patient with a metallic mitral valve attends the dermatological surgery department for an excision of a small nodular basal cell carcinoma on his chest. What should be the most appropriate action with regards to antibiotic prophylaxis for his metallic valve?

choices.A: A one-week course of penicillin after the procedure
choices.C: Penicillin and metronidazole single doses should be given
choices.E: Single penicillin dose one hour prior to the procedure

explanation: The current consensus is that dermatological surgical procedures confe, a low risk for endocarditis, and therefore, no prophylactic antibiotics are required. An assessment should however, still take place based on individual circumstances.

question: Which of the following presents with 'buttonholing' or 'dimple sign' on lateral pressure?
explanation: Dermatofibromas are firm, indurated, but mobile common mesenchymal lesions. Lateral compression of dermatofibroma produces a dimple-like depression in the overlying skin ( buttonholing ).

question: Which of the following alopecias has a predominantly neutrophilic infiltrate?
explanation: A predominantly neutrophilic infiltrate is found in folliculitis decalvans and dissecting cellulitis of the scalp. A lyrnphocytic infiltrate is found in lichen planopilaris, alopecia mucinosa, cutaneous lupus erythematosus, alopecia areata and pseudopelade of Brocq, though in the latter there may be little inflammation present. Early acne necrotica and erosive pustular dermatosis can have a mixed nl::!utrophilic and lymphocytic infiltrate.

question: Which of the following stain positively for cytokeratin?
explanation: Nodular amyloidosis is a rare primary cutaneous amyloidosis caused by the deposition of the AL amyloids produced by infiltrate of plasma cells. It Is therefore often regarded as a plasmacytoma. The other two types of cutaneous amyloidosis (macular and lichenoid) result from damaged keratinocytes; therefore they stain positively for cytokeratins. Carcinoma en cuirasse is cutaneous metastasis from breast carcinoma, this like other epithelial tumours stain positively for cytokeratins. 94 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: Which of the following is associated with an abnormal lipid profile?
explanation: With the exception of xanthomata disseminatum, and verucciform xanthomas, all other types of xanthomas are associated with an abnormal lipid profile. Eruptive xanthomata are often associated with elevated triglycerides as opposed to increased cholesterol levels in the other forms of xanthomata. Xanthomata disseminatum is a histiocytic disorder.

question: Which of the following organisms causes cutaneous larva migrans?
explanation: Cutaneous larva migrans is a pruritic eruption that is caused by the nematode hookworm Ankylostoma brazilense (and in some occasions Ankylostoma caninum), which is deposited in dogs and cats faeces. It clinically presents with serpiginous vesicular burrows that migrate slowly. The worm cannot penetrate the basement membrane. Stronglyoides stercoralis, another nematode, causes cutaneous larva currens which presents similarly with serpiginous urticaria! burrows on the buttocks or trunk. This worm however can penetrate the basement membrane and can affect the lungs and the gastrointestinal tract. When it does involve the lungs it may cause Loeffler s syndrome (pulmonary eosinophilia). Schistosomes may cause schistosomiasis and swimmer s itch. Mycobacterium marinum causes fish tank granuloma presenting with red to purple coloured nodules and plaques with sporotrichoid spread. A further difference between Stronglyoides and Ankylostoma is that the latter migrates slowly and Stronglyoides typically migrate fast. 95 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: In which of the following types of angioedema is the C4 level usually within the normal range?

choices.A: Acquired angioedema associated with B-cell lymphoma

explanation: An easy way to remember this is that all types of angioedema, with the exception of hereditary angioedema type Ill, angioedema as part of urticaria, and ACE inhibitor angiooedema are usually associated with low levels of C4. In hereditary angioedema type I, Cl esterase inhibitor levels are reduced, however in type II the Cl esterase inhibitor levels may be normal or elevated but the functional Cl inhibitor activity is decreased. Type Ill hereditary angioedema is exceptionally rare. and is associated with normal levels of both C4 and Cl esterase inhibitor. It is caused by mutation in factor XII. Type Ill hereditary angioedema is mostly seen in female patients and can be aggravated by oestrogens. Diagnosis is often difficult and requires identification offactor XII mutation. Acquired angioedema can occur secondary to lymphoproliferative disorders, or systemic lupus erythematosus. This is associated with low levels of both C4 and Cl esterase inhibitor levels and a positive anti-Clq antibody. The presence of anti-Clq antibody will help differentiate acquired angioedema (secondary to lymphoproliferative disorders or systemic lupus erythematosus) frcm hereditary angioedema in new cases where there is no family history.

question: In which of the following conditions is there typically no dyskeratosis at the suprabasal layer?
explanation: In Hailey-Hailey disease, there is acantholysis with usually little or no dyskeratosis. Other acantholytic disorders in the absence of dyskeratosis include: pemphigus vulgaris, pemphigus vegetans and the acantholytic variant of actinic keratosis. Conditions that can have both acantholysis and dyskeratosis include Darier s disease, Grover s disease, paraneoplastic pernphigus and warty dyskeratoma. It is worth mentioning that in Hailey-Hailey disease, direct immunofluorescence is negative, which differentiates this condition from pemphigus vulgaris.

question: At which level does lm NaCl cause a split in the skin?
explanation: Lamina lucida is the weakest part of the basement membrane. 96 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: A-40 year old man presents with fever c1nd red/purple tumid plaque 0,1 the face for 3 days. A skin biopsy shows papillary dermal oedema and a dense, diffuse neutrophilic infiltrate in the reticular dermis. What is the most common malignancy associated with this presentation?
explanation: Acute febrile neutrophilic dermatosis (Sweet s syndrome), is a reactive process. Abrupt onset of tender, red-to-purple papules coalesce to form plaques. Commonest sites include upper extremities, face, or neck. The rash is accompanied by fever and peripheral neutrophilia. Causes include hematopoietic malignancies (most commonly acute myeloid leukemia), non-hematologic malignancies; e.g. genitourinary, breast, and gastrointestinal cancers, infections most often involving the upper respiratory tract, drugs and systemic illnesses.

question: Which of the following is not a physical urticaria?
explanation: Other forms of physical urticarias include: cholinergic, vibratory, aquagenic and exercise-induced urticaria (exercise following the ingestion of shell fish and wheat are the commonest triggers). Hereditary angioedema should be considered in isolated angioedema unresponsive to anti-histamines or corticosteroids. ,., Low complement 4 levels are always found during the attacks (except in type 3 hereditary angioedema).

question: A 30-year old woman developed erythematous patches and plaques on her trunk. These were associated with mild pruritus and progressed to become indurated and oedematous with few plaques developing blisters. She reported that previous patches and plaques resolved after several weeks leaving a green hue. She had no mucosal involvement and laboratory investigations showed marked eosinophilia. A skin biopsy showed oedema, flame figures and an eosinophilic dermal infiltrate. Direct immunotluoresence was negative. The diagnosis is
explanation: The history, clinical findings, histology and the presence of an eosinophilia fit with the diagnosis of eosinophilic cellulitis (Well s syndrome). The condition can be associated with Infections, ulcerative colitis, lymphoma and leukaemia. Localized areas of eosinophilic cellulitis have been reported at injection sites of anti-TNF drugs. Topical or systemic corticosteroids are the treatment of choice. 97 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: A 3-month old baby of consanguineous parents suffered severe sunburn following a limited exposure to sunlight. Examination showed dry skin but otherwise no abnormalities. There is no family history of photosensitivity. Which condition should be suspP.cted and looked for?
explanation: Xeroderma pigmentosum is an autosomal recessive disorder characterized by marked photosensitivity, dry skin (hence the name xeroderma), abnormal freckling (hence pigmentosum) and a markedly increased risk of cutaneous neoplasms. A less severe form exist called variant form of XP. In XP marked sensitivity is to the UVB range is present hence the easy sunburns. XP should always be considered in any baby who suffers easy sunburns and/or the presence of freckling under the age of 2 years.

question: Which of the following does not trigger or worsen porphyria cutanea tarda (PCT)?
explanation: Serial phlebotomy is a treatment for PCT which can give clinical and biochemical remission and is particularly helpful in PCT patients with iron overload or haemochromatosis. Low dose hydroxychloroquine (e.g. 200 mg twice weekly) can be used particularly in patients with normal or low iron levels. Other triggers for PCT include hepatitis B/C, genetic mutation for the uroporphyrinogen decarboxylase enzyme {the familial form), and rarely hepatocellular carcinoma. Although PCT is the commonest cutaneous porphyria, variegate porphyria should always be excluded as this can be associated with fatal acute attacks and may present with cutaneous features similar to PCT.

question: Rifampicin may be an effective treatment for which of the following types of pruritus
explanation: Rifampicin is an inducer of hepatic enzymes and can be effective in the treatmer.t of cholestatic pruritus. Other treatments include cholestyramine and opioid receptor antagonists such as naltrexone. UVB phototherapy, naltrexone and gabapentin can be used in uraemic pruritus. 98 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: Which of the following treatments is recommended as first-line in the treatment of vulval lichen sclerosus (LS) according to the British Association of Dermatologists guidelines
explanation: Clobetasol proprionate ointment is recommended as first-line treatment in vulval LS. Although, all the other treatments can be used in this condition, very potent topical corticosteroids should be used first-line. Suspect a concomitant allergic contact dermatitis to perfumes, topical anaesthetics and c:orticosteroids in resistant or eczematized cases, in particular with chronic symptoms and prolonged use of multiple topical agents.

question: A patient with severe psoriasis who is currently well-controlled on the anti- TNF biologic Etanercept (Enbrel) is planning to travel abroad and has asked your advice with regards to immunisations. Which vaccine is safe in this context?
explanation: Knowledge about vaccines in immunosuppressed patients is important as more patients are rec0iving anti-TNF therapy in dermatology. Live vaccines must be avoided in patients who are receiving therapy with anti-TNF and these include: measles, mumps, rubella, small pox, yellow fever, dengue fever, BCG, polio, rabies, typhoid and varicella. Pneumococcal vaccine can be used safely in this patient.

question: Of which of the following conditions is livedo reticularis not a feature?
explanation: Kawasaki s disease is a medium-vessel vasculitis characterized by fever, conjunctiva! involvement, cervical lymphadenopathy, maculo-papular eruption on trunk and strawberry tongue. Other causes of livedo reticularis include polyarteritis nodosa, phaeochromocytoma, multiple sclerosis and amantadine use. A physiological variant exist- mainly following cold exposure -which disappears with re-warming.

question: Which of the following statements regarding leukaemia cutis is incorrect?

choices.A: Children with leukaemia are more likely to be affected than adults
choices.B: Cutaneous signs can appear prior to systemic involvement
choices.C: Mostly associated with acute myeloid leukaemias
choices.D: Portends a good prognosis for the :eukaemia
choices.E: Presence of leukaemia cutis is often associated with extra-medullary haemo poiesis

correct_text: Portends a good prognosis for the :eukaemia
explanation: Leukaemia cutis is often associated with a poor prognosis and may precede the detection of systemic disease when it is then referred to as a leukaemia cutis . Treatment is very challenging and is mainly palliative. 99 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: A 5-month old boy presented with a 6-week history of multiple tense vesicles and bullae appearing on the face, abdomen and scrotum. These are painless and some are arranged in an annular configuration resembling a "crown of jewels". No mucosa! involvement is present and a biopsy showed a subepidermal bulla with dense neutrophilic infiltrate. Which of the following statements regarding this condition is true?

choices.B: Histology typically shows a dense eosinophilic infiltrate
choices.D: Systemic corticosteroids are the first-line treatment of choice
choices.E: The disease is very rare in children

explanation: Linear lgA disease is the commonest bullous disorder in children. Mucous membrane involvement may occur in half of the patients. Dapsone remains the first-line treatment of choice. Subepidermal infiltrate is predominantly neutrophilic. Drugs can cause a similar disease in adults (drug-induced linear lgA disease) with vancomycin being tile commonest. Other vesiculo-bullous disorders in childhood include: congenital HSV, congenital varicella, bullous impetigo, scabies, toxic epidermal necrolysis, staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome, thermal burns, incontinentia pigmenti, epidermolysis bullosa, neonatal pemphigus vulgaris (from the mother), bullous pemphigoid, bullous mastocytosis and bullous congenital ichthyoslform erythroderma.

question: Trachyonychia is a recognised feature of which of the following
explanation: Trachyonychia - sand paper appearance and roughening of the nails. Spontaneous resolution commonly occurs. Other causes of trachonychia include: idiopathic, pemphigus vulgaris, psoriasis, lichen planus and eczema.

question: Which of the following does not portend a poor prognosis in alopecia areata?
explanation: Other poor prognostic factors include family history and chronicity. Differential diagnoses include telogen effluvium, anagen effluvium, trichotillomania, loose anagen syndrome, drug-induced alopecia, systemic lupus erythematosus, syphilis and tinea capitis.

question: Which of the following inherited forms of epidermolysis bullosa is associated with mutations of the gene coding for type VII collagen {COL7Al)?
explanation: Epidermolysis bullosa simplex- mutation in Keratins 5/14. Hemi-desmosomal epidermoly:;is bullosa- Epldemolysis bullosa with muscular dystrophy-mutation in PLEC1, EB with pyloric atresia-mutation in ITGB4/ITGA6. Junctional epidermolysis bullosa- mutation in LAMB3/LAMA3/LAMG2. Dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa- mutation in COL7Al. Kindler syndrome- mutation in KINDL Ectodermal dysplasia-skin fragility- mutation in PKPl. 100 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: Which of the following is the commonest clinical subtype of basal cell carcinoma?
explanation: Roughly 80% of all basal-cell carcinomas occur on the head and neck. In addition to the classic rodent ulcer with an indurated edge and ulcerated centre (nodular or cystic), superficial, morphoeic, and pigmented bzsal-cell carcinomas are other common subtypes. 10--40% of basal-cell carcinomas contain a mixed pattern of two or more of these histological subtypes, drawing attention to the need for a clinicopathological diagnosis. By contrast with r.odulocystic basal-cell carcinoma-which is the most common subtype, usually presenting on the head and neck-superficial basal-cell carcinomas predominantly present on the trunk. 5% of all basal-cell carcinomas are morphoeic lesions, which have ill-defined borders, can be difficult to diagnose clinically, and often present late.

question: One of the following syndromes does not predispose to cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma?
explanation: The following are syndromes predisposing to cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma: Xeroderma pigmentosum - autosomal recessive; multiple epidermal skin cancers in childhood; increased susceptibility to DNA damage; abnormal DNA base excision repair. Albinism - part or complete failure to produce melanin in the skin and eyes. Muir-Torre syndrome- autosomal dominant; germline mutations in genes involved in DNA mismatch repair; sebaceous neoplasms in association with internal malignancy. KID (keratosis, icthyosis, deafness) syndrome - development of invasive squamous cell carcinoma within dysplastic lesions. Dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa - autosomal recessive mechano-bullous disorder; mutations in the human type VII collagen gene (COL.7A1). Fanconi anaemia - autosomal recessive; congenital malformations; bone-marrow failure; development of squamous-cell carcinoma and other cancers. Rothmund-Thompson syndrome - autosomal recessive; progressive poikiloderma including alopecia, dystrophic teeth and nails, juvenile cataracts, short stature, hypogonadism, and bone defects. Werner syndrome - early ageing; excess cancer risk; high incidence of type 2 diabetes mellitus; early atherosclerosis; ocular cataracts; osteoporosis. Others - Hereditary non-polyposis coli; dyskeratosis congenit:1; Huriez syndrome; Li-Fraumeni syndrome and chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis. 101 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: Which of the following is not a poor prognostic factor in basal cell carcinomas?
explanation: Factors determining poor prognosis in basal cell carcinomas include: morphoeic lesions, tumour size> 5 cm (giant), deeper lesions, centrofacial and ears, infiltrative and micronodular histological subtypes, histological features of aggression including perineural or perivascular involvement, or both and recurrent lesions.

question: Which of the following is not a neutrophilic dermatosis
explanation: Erythema multiforme is a reactive self-limiting condition which is predominantly lymphocytic. Other examples of neutrophilic dermatoses include subcorneal pustular dermatosis and bowel-associated dermatosis-arthritis syndrome. The neutrophilic dermatoses can be associated with internal disease/haematological malignancies and often respond well to systemic corticosteriods.

question: A geographic tongue can be found in all the following conditioi1s except
explanation: Down s syndrome is associated with macroglossia. No specific treatment is required for geographic tongue.

question: A 39-year old man developed fever, neutrophilia and a rash, which started in the groins and lower abdomen 10 days after he was prescribed amoxicillin for a presumed chest infection. The rash consisted of small pinhead-sized non-follicular pustules on a background of erythema. The rash desquamated after 2 weeks leaving normal-looking background skin. Liver and kidney function tests were all within normal range. There was no mucosal in1 1olvement. What is the most likelv diagnosis?

choices.B: Drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms

explanation: The history and clinical findings are typical of AGEP (acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis) which is a self-limiting drug eruption that often begins in the flexi;res. Pustular psoriasis is the main differential but a history of previous psoriasis and the absence of any drug intake can help differentiate the two conditions. An eosinophilic infiltrate in the biopsy can sometimes be helpful and would point towards AGEP. Acanthosis and papillomatosus are often seen in pustular psoriasis and rarely in AGEP, which can also aid in the differentiation. Drug eruptions that are accompanied by fever include AGEP, toxic epidermal necrolysis/Stevens-Johnson syndrome and DRESS. 102 Section 1: Answer.. & Comments

question: A 45-year old man presents to the rheumatologist with severe psoriasis and joint pains. Which of the following is not a recognised form of psoriatic arthritis?
explanation: Psoriatic artliropathy can present in the following forms: -Distal int rphal,rngeal joint (commonest}. -Oligoarticular asymmetrical. -Polyarticular symmetrical (rheumatoid arthritis like). -Spondylitis and sacroiliitis. -Arthritis mutilans.

question: Which of the following is not a risk factor for the development of Bowen's disease?
explanation: Gorlin s syndrome predisposes to multiple basal cell carcinomas and not Bowen s disease or squamous cell carcinoma. Other features of Gorlin s syndrome include palmoplantar pits, odontogenic jaw cysts, frontal bossing, medullohlastomas, lipomas and t,ypogonadism. HPV can cause Bowen s disease and is one of the aetiologic factors for the development of squamous cell carcinomas in transplant patients.

question: Which of the following is not a risk factor for (recurrent) cellulitis?
explanation: Although alcohol and smoking are thought to increase the possible risk for cellulitis, this has not been proven in any study. Lymphoedema is the strongest risk factor for the development of cellulitis followed by leg ulcers. The risk of cellulitis increases after each episode due to post-cellulitis residual oedema (mostly secondary lymphoedema} and all the above mentioned factors need to be tal<en into account when managing patients with cellulitis. 103 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: A 55-year-old woman presents with a 5-week history of burning sensation of her feet. Weight bearing was extremely painful. The pain was only p;;irtially relieved on cold water soaks. Examination showed erythema of the soles of the feet which was very tender to touch. Pedal pulsations were normal. She had a history of duodenal ulceration for which she took omeprazole. Heamatological investigations showed haemoglobin of 12.Sg/dl, normal white cell and differential count and a platelet count of 550 xl03 /1. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Erythromelalgia is characterised by intense burning pain and erythema (marked redness) of the extremities. Erythromelalgia is classified into primary and secondary or early-onset and late- onset forms. Primary erythromelalgia develops spontaneously and is also known as idiopathic erythromelalgia as the cause remains unknown. Secondary erythromelalgia can be secondary to myeloproliferative disorders, neurological diseases (e.g. multiple sclerosis, peripheral neuropathy), or autoimmune diseases (e.g. lupus, diabetes mellitus). The most common cause of secondary erythromelalgia are myeloproliferative disorders including polycythaemia vera, and essential thrombocythaemla. Erythromelalgia may precede the diagnosis of myeloprollferative disorders in 85% of cases. it is characterised by red, painful, warm hands or feet. Chilblain-like lesions can occur in myeloproliferative disorders but are cold to touch. The burning symptoms are exacerbated by warming or hanging the limb downward, and relieved with cooling and elevation. Systemic treatments include aspirin, serotonin re-uptake inhibitors - venlafaxine, sertraline, fluoxetine, paroxetine; tricyclic antidepressants - amitriptyline, imipramine, gabapentin, nifedipine, diltiazem and prostaglandins - misoprostol.

question: The mortality related to methotrexate has been primarily attributed to
explanation: Idiosyncratic reactions can occur with any dose and are therefore dose- independent. Oral ulcers may indicate methotrexate toxicity or folate deficiency. Methotrexate should be used with caution in renal impairment.

question: A 30-year old patient with polycystic ovarian syndrome was referred for laser treatment of facial hirsutism. The following hair-skin combination is considered best for laser treatment
explanation: Skin phototype 2 - dark terminal hair is considered the best combination for successful laser hair removal with the currently available lasers and light devices including intense pulsed light, long pulsed Nd:YAG, diode and Alexandrite lasers. This combination results in best clinical outcomes with least side effects. Skin phototype 1 patients rarely have dark terminal hairs. 104 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: A 30-year old patient with polycystic ovarian syndrome was referred for laser treatment of facial hirsutism. She is currently using topical eflornithine cream. Your advice, based on current recommendation Is

choices.B: Continue treatment with eflornithine cream, but stop for few days after laser treatment
choices.C: Stop eflornithine cream for 3 months prior to laser treatment
choices.D: Stop eflornithine cream for 6 months prior to laser treatment
choices.E: Stop eflornithine cream for 12 months prior to laser treatment

explanation: Available evidence suggests that addition of eflornithine to laser treatment results in a more rapid and complete reduction of unwanted facial hair in women when the combination is used for up to 6 months.

question: A-45 year old woman wants treatment of her tattoo. Which laser would be the most appropriate for the treatment of her red professional tattoo?
explanation: Q5:Nd:Yag (532 nm) emits green light and is the treatment of chioce for red tattoos.

question: A 25-year old woman has facial pigmentation, which has been formally diagnosed as melasma. Which of the following is the recommended laser treatment for melasma?
explanation: Treatment of melasma with pigment specific lasers is disappointing and as such is not recommended.

question: Which of the following types of botulinum toxin is most commonly used in the treatment of hyperkinetic facial lines?
explanation: There are seven distinct serotypes of botulinum toxin: A, B, Cl, D, E, F and G.

question: A 40-year old woman attends for botulinum toxin injection to treat glabellar lines. Which of the following concurrent treatment would not be considered a contra- indication for botulinum toxin injection?
explanation: The listed drugs can potentiate the action of botox, which should be avoided if the patient is on any of these medications.

question: A 60-year old patient is interested in treatment of his deep glabellar lines. Which of the following is considered the safest in the treatment of deep glabellar lines?
explanation: Local skin necrosis has been reported following deep glabellar injection of bovine collagen induced vascular occlusion. Loss of vision due to arterial embolization has been reported with both bovine collagen and autologous fat injected into the glabellar region. 105 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: Which of the following chemical peels is associated with a risk of cardiac toxicity?
explanation: Cardiac arrhythmias and laryngeal oedema have been reported with phenol peels. Precautions recommended at the time of phenol peels inc.lude appropriate analgesia, adequate hydration, and availability of cardiac monitoring and resuscitation equipment.

question: A 58-year-old woman is admitted with deep vein thrombosis. Three days e1-fter being commenced on warfarin she develops necrotic and painful bullae on her thighs. What should be the next step in management?
explanation: Warfarin causes inactivation of clotting factors II, VII, IX and X and proteins C and S. Cond,tions such as inherited deficiency of protein C, protein S or factor V Leiden, mutations in methylene tetra hydro to:ate redu<.tase gene causing hyperhomocysteinaemla, antithrombin Ill deficiency or the presence of antiphospholipid antibodies predispose to warfarin-induced skin necrosis. The first step in management is to stop the warfarin therapy. Other measures include administration of vitamin Kor protein C concentrates.

question: A 58-year old man complains of blurring of vision. He has been using a medication for hyperhidrosis. Which of the following Is the most likely cause of his symptoms?
explanation: Glycopyrrolate is an anticholinergic agent which can be used In the treatment of compensatory, craniofacial, and diabetic gustatory hyperhidrosis. It acts by preventing the acetylcholine-induced stimulation of the sweat gland receptors. Its inability to cross the blood brain barrier, results in fewer side effects. Systemically administered anticholinergic agents may result in dry mouth, visual disturbances, urinary retention and urgency, flushing and constipation. 106 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: A 56-year old patient is commenced on ciclosporin for psoriasis. Which of the following is true regarding monitoring of ciclosporin therapy?

choices.A: Clclosporln dose should be reduced if serum creatinine increases by 30% above the baseline value
choices.B: Cliclosporin bloavailablllty remains uniform irrespective of the brand used
choices.C: GFR measurement should be carried out every 6 months for patients on long term clclosporin
choices.D: Intake of grapefruit Juice should be encouraged
choices.E: Rise In blood pressure always necessitates additional drug therapy 1R

correct_text: Clclosporln dose should be reduced if serum creatinine increases by 30% above the baseline value
explanation: Ciclosporin dose should be reduced if serum creatinine increases by 30% above the baseline value (even if this increase is within the laboratory normal range). Grapefruit juice interferes with gut cytochrome P-450 enzymes, which are important in metabolizing ciclosporin and therefore it should not be administered simultaneously with ciclosporin. Only a minority of patients (5-12%) develop new-onset hypertension during short-course ciclosporin therapy, and the overwhelming majority of these cases respond to dose reduction and/or anti-hypertensive medication. As ciclosporin nephropathy is closely related to duration of therapy, GFR should be assessed annually i11 patients receiving long-term continuous ciclosporin treatment. Ciclosporin has formulation-dependent bloavallabllity with a wide inter-individual variability in absorption. Appropriate brand of ciclosporin should be consistently dispensed.

question: Which of the following drugs is implicated in the causation of ingrown toe nails?
explanation: Ingrowing toenails can be caused by prescribed medications Including retinolds, indinavir and methotrexate.

question: A 65-yea, old woman presents with blisters on the back of her hands. Her rash Is photosensitive and you suspect that she may have porphyria and carry out a porphyrin screen which is normal. You take a detailed drug history. Which of the following is the most likely cause of her rashi'
explanation: The clinical picture is that of pseudoporphyria-porphyria cutanea tarda-like photosensitive blistering and skin fargility. No hypertrichosis, hyperpigmentation or sclerodermoid changes are seen. Causes of pseudoporphyria include- NSAID s, tetracyclines, haemodialysis, tanning booths, thiazides and frusemide.

question: A 65-year old patient presents with velvety pigmented changes in axillary skin and similar changes around the perioral area. You are worried that he may have an internal malignancy. Which of the following is the most common malignancy associated with these cutaneous changes?
explanation: Gastric cancer is the commonest tumour associated with malignant acanthosis nigricans. The changes may regress if the tumour, usually an adenocarcinoma of the stomach or bowel, is removed. 107 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: A 55-year-old man is admitted to the hepatology ward and is undergoing investigations for jaundice. Your hepatologist colleague asks you to have a look at his naiis, which display a bluish discolouration of the lanulae. Which of the following is associated with azure nails?
explanation: Azure lanulae, a bluish colour of the lanular portion of nails, occurs In hepatolenticular degeneration (Wilson s disease). Similar nail changes and corneal changes resembling WIison s Kayser-Fleischer rings may also be evident in patients with argyria or after treatment with busulfan or antimalarials.

question: A 45-year old patient is diagnosed with Crohn's disease. He has apthous ulceration. Other cutaneous features of Crohn's disease include all of the following except
explanation: Aphthous ulcers may be a presenting feature of Crohn s disease. Oral granulomatous nodules are commonly seen in Crohn s disease, where they may coalesce to give a cobblestone appearance. Granulomatous cheilitis may predate bowel disease by ;;everal years. Granulomas may also occur in the perineum, at colostomy and ileostomy sites, and in association with scars, sinuses, and fistulas. Granulomas can occur at sites not contiguous with the bowel, such as the trunk and limbs: the so-called metastatic cutaneous Crohn s disease.

question: A 2-year old Caucasian boy is referred to the Paediatric dermatology clinic with the appearance of a kinky, wavy hair on the scalp. You carry out hair pluck test and find tightly coiled hair on microscopy. Which other system involvement is to be excluded?
explanation: Woolly hair is the presence of kinl-. Y, wavy hair on the scalp of persons of non-African or Negroid background. Microscopically, the hairs are tightly coiled. The unruly hair presents at birth or in infancy, usually as a solitary problem inherit d in an autosomal dominant fashion. Mutations in the genes for the desmosomal proteins plakoglobin (Naxos disease) or desmoplakin give rise to the triad of woolly hair, striate palmar-plantar keratoderma, and cardiomyopathy. Both recessive and dominant patterns of inheritance have been reported. Assessment of cardiac status should be performed In all children presenting with generalized woolly hair. 108 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: A forensic pathologist is examining hair for suspected poisoning. Chronic exposure and cumulative toxicity of which of the following chemicals can be identified in this way?
explanation: Mercury in1:oxication can lead to hair loss with or without neurological symptoms. Elevated mercury levels can be found in hair, blood, or urine. Boric acid intoxication also results in hair loss. Gcistrointestinal, central nervous system, and renal symptoms; a hemorrhagic diathesis; and exfoliation or bullae are also seen with boric acid intoxication. Blood boric acid levels are elevated In affected patients. Thallium poisoning leads to dramatic hair loss, with complete epilation occurring 2 to 3 weeks after intoxication. Neurologic symptoms including irritability, dysesthesia, ataxia, convulsions, and coma can also result following thallium intoxication. Blood and urine levels of thallium are positive at the time of acute poisoning. In contrast to the above, arsenic exposure does not cause hair loss. Arsenic concentrates in the hair, which fac!lltates a diagnosis long after intoxication may have occurred.

question: A 12-year old patient is diagnosed with alopecia areata. His parents are interested in knowing the prognosis. The following are associated with a poor prognosis in alopecia areata except
explanation: Spontaneous remission is common in most patients with localised patches of alopecia areata. Poor prognostic factors in alopecia areata include alopecia totalis and universalis, ophiasis pattern, onset in childhood, loss of body hair, nail Involvement, atopy, and a positive family history for alopecia areata.

question: A-40 year old man presents with androgenetic alopecia. He has heard about topical minoxidil solution. Which of the following statements regarding the use of topical minoxidil solution in androgenetic alopecia is not true?

choices.B: Any hair gained is lost within 4 to 6 months of stopping minoxidil treatment
choices.C: Mean increase in hair density of 10-12% can be achieved
choices.D: Minoxidil is effective in treating vertex balding
choices.E: Minoxidil is not effective in treating frontotemporal recession

explanation: Up to 60 percent of men show improvement in vertex balding using 5 % minoxidil lotion. A mean increase in hair density of 10 to 12% is obtained. The response rate with 2 % lotion are lower (the recommended concentration in women). Any hair gained is lost within 4 to 6 months of stopping treatment. Minoxidil is not effective in treating frontotemporal recession. 109 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: A 65-year old man is seen with transverse depressions in nail plate. He has been undergoing cancer chemotherapy. Where does the abnormality originate?
explanation: Beau s lines result from a temporary arrest of proximal nail matrix proliferation. These appear as transverse grooves in the nail plate that move distally with nai: growth. Multiple Beau s lines in the same nail indicates repetitive insults. Beau s lines at the same level in several nails suggest a systemic cause. The time of the insult leading to Beau s lines can be dated by measuring the distance of the groove from the proximal nail fold. Causes of Beau s lines include local traurr:a, or can be related to local cutaneous disease, particularly eczema and paronychia. Systemic causes include drugs (especially chemotherapy), high fever, viral illness, surgery, and peripheral ischemia.

question: You see a 35-year old patient with longitudinal melanonychia affecting 2 fingernails. Which of the following is not a recognised cause?
explanation: Melanonychia signifies the presence of melanin in the nail plate and appears as a single or longitudinal brown to black band. Caused by activation or proliferation of nail matrix melanocytes. Causes include racial, acquired immunodeficiency syndrome, inflammatory nail disorders, certain medic.ations, Addison s disease, pregnancy, Laugier-Huntziker syndrome, and trauma. Single nail melanonychia may be secondary to nail matrix naevus or melanoma.

question: A 35-year old patient with Darier's disease presents with some changes affecting the fingernails. You expect to see some or all of the changes expect;
explanation: Key features of nail disease in Darier s disease include longitudinal erythconychia, longitudinal leukonychia associated with distal nail plate nicking (V-shaped), and subungual hyperkeratotic papules. 110 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: A 60-year old woman is referred with scaly, crusted erosions on the malar area of the face and seborrhoeic areas. Skin biopsy shows acanthcilysis in the superficial epidermis just below the stratum corneum and in the granular layer. Antinuclear antibodies are detected on serological testing. Which of the following is the correct diagnosis?
explanation: Senear-llsher syndrome or pemphigus erythematosus is a localized form of pemphigus foliaceous. Scaly and crusted lesions occur across the malar area of the face and in other seborrheic areas. Pemphigus erythematosus may remain localized for years, or it may evolve into more generalized pemphigus foliaceous. Many patients with pemphigus erythematosus show serologic findings suggestive of systemic lupus erythematosus, especially the presence of anti-nuclear antibodies.

question: A 70-year old man is admitted with painful stomatitis and a polymorphous cutaneous eruption with a predominantly blistering rash. A skin biopsy showed Intra-epidermal acantholysis and direct immunofluoresence showed deposition of immunoglobulin G and complement in the epidermal intercellular spaces, and granular/linear complement deposition along the epidermal basement membrane zone. Which of the following is the most common associated diagnosis?
explanation: Paraneoplastic pemphigus is an autoimmune disorder. It is almost always linked to an underlying lymphoproliferative disorder. Its features include painful stomatitis and a polymorphous cutaneous eruption including blistering, lichenoid, erythema multiforme-like lesions. Histologic findings include acantholysis, lichenoid, or interface changes. Direct immunofluorescence demonstrates deposition of immunoglobulin G (lgG) and complement in the epidermal intercellular spaces, and often granular/linear complement deposition along the epidermal basement membrane zone. In addition to binding the cell surface of skin and mucosae in a pattern typical for pemphigus, serum auto-antibodies also bind to simple, columnar, and transitional epithelia. These serum auto-antibodies identify desmogleins 1 and 3 and additionally desmoplakins, envoplakin, and periplakin. Most commonly associated diseases include non-Hodgkin lymphoma {NHL), chronic lymphocytic leukemia, and Castleman s disease. 111 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: A 45-year-old patient who was commenced on lamotrigine for epilepsy presents with a morbilliform skin rash, fever, facial oedema and lymphadenopathy. Which of the following statements with regards to this drug reaction is incorrect?

choices.A: Atypical lymphocytosis with subsequent eosinophilia may occur during the initial phases
choices.B: Central nervous system involvement is never seen
choices.C: Cross-reactivity to the other aromatic anticonvulsants may occur
choices.D: The reaction most frequently occurs on first exposure to the drug
choices.E: The susceptibility to develop this reaction may be familial

correct_text: Central nervous system involvement is never seen
explanation: Hypersensitivity syndrome reaction (HSR), also called drug reaction with eopsinophilia and systemtic symptoms (DRESS syndrome), is the presence of exanthematous eruption in conjunction with fever and internal organ involvement (e.g. liver, kidney, central nervous system) which occurs in app oximate:y 1 in 3000 exposures to age;its such as aromatic anti-convulsants, lamotrigine, sulfonamide antibiotics, dapsone, nitrofurantoin, nevirapine, minocycline, and allopurinol. DRESS occurs most frequently on first exposure to the drug, with initial symptoms starting 1 to 6 weeks after exposure. Fever and malaise are often the presenting symptoms. Atypical lymphocytosis with subsequent eosinophilia may occur during the initial phases of the reaction in some patients. Most patients have an exanthematous eruption. Internal organ involvement car, be asymptomatic. The chemically reactive metabolites of aromatic anti-convulsants that are produced are detoxified by epoxide hydroxylases. If detoxification is defective, however, one of the metabolites may act as a hapten and initiate an immune response, stimulate apoptosis, or cause cell necrosis directly. Approximately 70-75% of patients who develop anticonvulsant HSR in response to one aromatic anti-convulsant show cross-reactivity to the other aromatic anti-convulsants. In vitro testing shows that there is a familial occurrence of HSR induced by anti- convulsants. Thus, counselling of family members and disclosure of risk is essential.

question: A-34 year old Asian man presents with a monomorphic pustular eruption on the face and limbs. Only a few papules and no comedones were seen. He was referred by the infectious diseases team, who had only recently commenced him on anti-tubercu lar therapy. Which of the following drugs is most commonly implicated?
explanation: Drug-induced acne may appear ;n atypical areas, such as on the arms and legs. The lesions are mostly monomorphous and comedones are usually absent. Topical tretinoin may be useful. Implicated drugs include iodides, bromides, adrenocorticotropic hormone, glucocorticoids, isoniazid, androgens, and lithium. 112 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: Which of the following conditions c;:in give a "pterygium" if the nail apparatus is affected?
explanation: V-shaped distal nick and leuko - or erythronychia can be seen in Darier s disease. Lichen str!atus may result in nail dystrophy and trachonychia but not pterygium. Hyperthyroidism is associated with onycholysis. l.ichen nitid•Js is not associated with any specific nail changes.

question: Latex can cross-react with all of the following except
explanation: Peanuts are legumes and can cross-react with beans, soya, peas and lentils. Cross-reaction with tree nuts may also occur. Cross-reaction of latex with certain fruits give rise to the latex-fruit allergy syndrome in which the symptoms are similar to the oral allergy syndrome that occurs due to the cross-reaction of birch pollen with certain fruits such as apples and pears. The symptoms are mainly of contact urticaria (type-1 allergy).

question: In order to be "eligible" for funding to use biological therapy in severe chronic plaque psoriasis the patient must have tried and failed at least 2 systemic therapies and have

choices.D: DLQI and PASI both are equal to or more than 10
choices.E: DLQI and PASI both less than 10

correct_text: DLQI and PASI both are equal to or more than 10
explanation: The current guidelines state that in order to be eligible for biological therapy a patient must have severe disease and have a DLQI and a PASI equal to or greater than 10. !ntolerance to or lack of response to systemic agents is an additional requirement. The NICE guidelines suggest that Infliximab can be considered when the PASI is equal to or greater than 20 and the DLQI is over 18.

question: Which of the following biological therapies for psoriasis is administered intravenously?
explanation: Infliximab is administered intravenously as a dose of 5 mg/kg at weeks 0, 2, 6 and every 8 weeks thereafter. Dosing of ustekinumab is also weight-based: (i} 45 mg for patients under 100 kg, and, (ii)90 mg for those over 100 kg. It is administered subcutaneously.

question: With regards to anti-TNF therapy in severe psoriasis in patients with congestive cardiac failure, the current British Association of Dermatologlsts recommendations are

choices.A: Avoidance in any New York Heart Association (NYHA) class
choices.C: Avoidance in NYHA class II and above
choices.D: Avoidance in NYHA class Ill and IV
choices.E: Safe to use with no risks in patients with cardiac failure

correct_text: Avoidance in NYHA class Ill and IV
explanation: Anti-TNF therapy should be avoided in patients with New York Heart Association (NYHA} class Ill and IV congestive cardiac failure. Avoidance should also include patients with NYHA class I or II who have an ejection fraction of less than 50%. 113 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: Which one of the following factors does not confer a higher risk of recurrence for basal cell carcinomas?

choices.C: Tumour around the lips or ears
choices.E: Tumour with poorly defined clinical margins

explanation: Recurrence risk for basal cell carcinomas depends on several factors including size, site, clinical margins, histological subtype/features of aggressive tumour, and failure of previous treatments. High-risk sites include areas around the eyes, nose, lips and ears. The presence of a metaplastic, Infiltrative, morphoeic or micro-nodular histological subtype is regarded as a high risk tumour.

question: Regarding the use of radiotherapy in basal cell carcinoma (BCC), which statement is false?

choices.A: Radiotherapy can be used as an adjuvant treatment
choices.B: Radiotherapy can be used in the treatment of primary BCC
choices.C: Suitable as a mode of treatment for radiorecurrent BCC
choices.D: Suitable as a mode of treatment for surgically recurrent BCC

correct_text: Suitable as a mode of treatment for radiorecurrent BCC
explanation: Radiorecurrent BCCs should not be retreated with radiotherapy and should be excised surgically. Radiotherapy may be more preferable as first-line therapy in elderly or infirm patients in whom surgery may not be possible.

question: Acitretin is a retinoid that can be used in psoriasis. Which of the following statements regarding this drug Is true?

choices.A: Combination with methotrexate increases the risk of hepatotoxicity
choices.B: Combination with tetracyclines increases the risk of benign intracranial hypertension
choices.C: Contraception should be continued for 2-3 years following discontinuation
choices.D: Hyperlipidaemia is one of the possible side-effects

explanation: Acitretin can be used in psoriasis, Darier s disease, keratoderrnas, pa Imo-plantar pustulosis, hyperkeratotic hand eczema, and severe congenital lchthyoses. The drug is very teratogenic and should not be considered in women of child-bearing age. In extreme cases when it has to be used in this group, contraception must be continued for at least 2-3 years following discontinuation of the drug.

question: Which of the following conditions or eruptions is not considered paraneoplastic?
explanation: Other paraneoplastic conditions include pruritus, acanthosis nigricans, Sweet s syndrome, Leser-Trelat sign, pal mar tylosis, acquired hypertrichosis lanuginosa, migratory thrombophlebitis and paraneoplastic pemphigus. Suspect malignancy in acanthosis nigrlcans in the presence of weight loss and normoglycaemia. 114 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: Which pattern of drug eruptions is the commonest?
explanation: A maculo-papular drug exanthem is the commonest pattern of drug reaction occurring mostly within 2 weeks of drug ingestion. Urticarial eruptions are the second most common followed by vasculitis. Other patterns of drug eruptions include generalized exanthematous pustulosis, photosensitivity, lichenoid eruptions, xerosis, hair loss, bullous and exfoliative. Some drugs can worsen existent skin diseases such as psoriasis.

question: Acquired ichthyosis can occur in which of the following?
explanation: Sudden-onset of acquired ichthyosis should alert the dermatologist to look for an underlying malignancy. Other causes include drugs and HIV infection.

question: Cutaneous sarcoidosis can clinically present as
explanation: Plaque-type sarcoidosis is the commonest cutaneous type followed by nodules. Other variants include ichthyotic, dystrophic nails, subcutaneous and scar sarcoidosis.

question: Mucin deposition is seen in which of the following cutaneous conditions?
explanation: Other conditions in which mucin deposition is found include reticular erythematous mucinosis, lichen myxoedema, sclerodermoid GVHD, granuloma annulare, and lupus erythematosus. Myxoid cyst is the commonest mucin deposition condition.

question: Which type of cryoglobulinaemia is not associated with hepatitis C infection?
explanation: Cryoglobulins are immunoglobulins that precipitate following cold exposure. Types II and III are called mixed cryoglobulinaemia and can be associated with hepatitis C, connective tissue diseases, HIV, and lymphoproliferative disorders. Type I is associated with lymphoproliferative disorders but not with hepatitis C. Suspect cryoglobulinaemia in the presence of a pernlo-like appearance of digits, reticulate leukocytoclastic cutaneous vasculitis and when the levels of C4 are reduced. 115 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: In which of the following conditions can calcinosis cutis develop?
explanation: Calcinosis cutis is a well-recognized complication of juvenile dermatomyositis although it may occur (less commonly) in the adult form. Juvenile dermatomyositis is not associated with an underlying malignancy (unlike the adult form). Other conditions in which calcinosis cutis may occur include hyperparathyroidism, pseudohypoparathyroidism and chronic renal failure.

question: In which of the following is poikiloderma a feature?
explanation: Poikiloderma consists of pigmentary changes, atrophy and telangiectasia. Other conditions in which poikiloderma may ooccur Include mycosis fungoides, Rothmund-Thomspson syndrome and Bloom s syndrome. Poikiloderma of Civatte is a benign finding secondary to the effects of ultraviolet radiation and fragrances - appearing on the sides of the neck.

question: Which of the following drugs is associated with acneiform eruption?
explanation: An acneiform eruption secondary to a drug typically presents with predominantly monomorphic papules and pustules with no comedones (excepting the pre-existing comedones). Other drugs that can give such an eruption include corticosteroids, androgens, phenytoin, isoniazid, haloperidol and sirolimus. The relatively new anti-cancer drugs (Epidermal Growth factor Receptor Antagonists) can give in addition to an acneiform eruption; xerosis, alopecia, pyogenic granuloma-like lesions in the digits and paronychia.

question: Which of the following benign lesions can arise from a congenital naevus sebaceous?
explanation: Naevus sebaceous represents a congenital hamartoma of sebaceous elements most commonly found on the scalp. Although it is present at birth, it acquires a verrucous appearance at puberty. Other lesions that may arise from it include basal cell carcinoma and trichoblastoma. 116 Section 1: Answer.; & Comments

question: "Collodion baby" is a clinical finding describing a new-born infant encased in an oily parchment-like shiny skin. This finding can occur in which of the following conditions?
explanation: Collodion membranes may resolve spontaneously or evolve into non-bullous ichthysioform erythroderma or lamellar ichthyosis. Complications m y include infections, dehydration and hypernataemia. Newborns with Netherton s syndrome typically present with an exfoliative erythroderma. Hay-Wells syndrome is an autosomal dominant condition which Is a type of ectodermal dysplasia caused by a mutation in the TP7PQL gene. The 2 features that differentiate Hay-Wells syndrome from other ectodermal dysplasias are the occurrence of clefting of the lip or palate and the fusion of the edges (often become fibrotic} of the upper and lower eyelids.

question: A 56-year old man With myeloid leukaemia developed deranged liver function tests, diarrhoea and a maculo-papular eruption involving the palms and soles with marked follicular accentuation. This occured within 60 days following an allogenic bone-marrow transplantation. The most likely diagnosis here is
explanation: Acute GVHD occurs within the first 100 days following an allogenic transplant tissue (mostly but not exclusively bone marrow) and typically presents with an exanthematous eruption most markedly on the palms and soles, hepatitis, diarrhoea and malaise. Occasionally erythroderma followed by an exfoliation can occur giving a clinical picture similar to toxic epidermal necrolysis. The most important differential diagnoses include a viral and drug-related exanthem and the eruption of lymphocyte recovery.

question: Which of the following alopecias is typically non-scarring?
explanation: Other causes of scarring alopecias include folliculitis Decalvans, erosive pustular dermatosis and pseudopelade. Non-scarring alopecias include anagen effluvium, alopecia areata, loose anagen syndrome and syphilitic alopecia (patchy with a moth-eaten appearance). In scarring alopecia the type of infiltrate (neutrophilic, lymphocytic or mixed) is also important pointer to the diagnosis. 117 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: Which of the following cutaneous manifestations can be associated with hepatitis C infection?
explanation: Hepatitis C infection can be associated with several cutaneous manifestations which include polyarteritis nodosa, lichen planus, erythema nodosum, cryoglobulinaemia (types II and Ill) and chronic urticaria. Hepatitis B and C should always be looked for in the work-up of porphyria i:utanea tarda.

question: Which of the following photosensitive or photo-aggravated conditions does not present with "blistering" following UV or visible light exposure?
explanation: Erythema multiforme can be aggravated following ultraviolet exposure (in particular if it was due to herpes simplex virus) and the photo-aggravated variant can be bullous in morphology. Other conditions resulting in blistering following UV exposure include pseudoporphyria and bullous lupus erytherr.atosus. Actinic prurigo presents with excoriated papules or nodules (sometimes with plaques or an eczematous appearance) but not with blistering.

question: A 7-year old boy presents with pruritic papules on the face and dorsal hands following exposure to the sunlight. The symptoms require a minimum of 20 minutes exposure and appe3r few hours afterwards. On examination there were excoriated papules on the nose, ears and cheeks with an excoriated lesion on the lower lip. Further history reveals conjunctiva! symptoms. There is no family history of photosensitive disorders. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: The history and findings of excoriated papules on the face with involvement of the nose and cheilitis is typical of actinic prurigo. Conjunctiva! involvement is common in this condition. Unlike PLE, this condition tends to worsen as summer progresses and patients do not develop tolerance. Hydroa vacciniforme presents with vesicles which become haemorri,agic leaving pock-like scars. Chronic actinic dermatitis is not seen in childhood and affects mostly middle-ageci and old men. Papules are the commonest morphological presentation of PLE {others ir,clude vesicles, urticaria!, and eczematous variants) but are usually not excoriated and clo not involve the lips and are not associated with conjunctiva! symptoms. 118 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: In which of the following photosensitive disorders is sensitivity to the visible wavelength always present?
explanation: All porphyrias are sensitive to the visible wavelength of the radiation, hence sunblocks that only block UVB and to a lesser degree UVA are largely ineffective in this condition. Solar urticaria is sensitive to predominantly UVA but the range of sensitivity can extend to involve both the UVB and visible light spectra. Around half of the patients with chronic actinic dermatitis exhibit photosensitivity in the visible wavelength.

question: In which of the following photosensitive disorders is monochromator reading nearly always abnormal?
explanation: Although any photosensitive disorder can have abnormal monochromator readings, these are nearly always (technique dependent) abnormal in chronic actinic dermatitis, solar urticaria, porphyria, and to a lesser degree drug-induced photosensitivity.

question: Which of the following - predominantly childhood - photosensitive disorders is not inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern?
explanation: Although actinic prurigo has a strong association with HLA-DRBl *0407, the condition is not inherited through the Mendelian pattern. Rothmund Thomson syndrome is associated with photosensitivity, poikiloderma, short stature, skeletal dysplasia and juvenile cataracts. The condition can predispose to squamous cell carcinomas and osteosarcomas. Bloom s syndrome is characterized by photosensitivity and poikiloderma but growth retardation is more marked and the risk of developing malignancies is much greater but these tend to be leukaemias early in life and solid organ tumours later.

question: Which of the following surfaces reflect ultraviolet rays the most?
explanation: Snow can reflect around 90% of the UV rays followed by water and sand. Sun protection advice should always include the risk of reflection from those surfaces. 119 Section 1: Answeri; & Comments

question: A 56-year old, normally fit and well, man presented with a 2 cm telangiectatic pearly lesion on the forehead but with rather indistinctive scar-like margin. What would be the most appropriate therapeutic intervention?

choices.E: Simple excision with a 4 mm margin

explanation: This is a morphoeic basal cell carcinoma and therefore Mohs micrographic surgery is the most appropriate intervention. Other indications for this type of surgery include recurrent basal cell carcinomas, large tumours (size > 2 cm), aggressive histology (metaplastic, infiltrative, morphoeic and micro-nodular) and high-risk sites (forehead and around the eyes, nose and ears).

question: A 23-year old woman presented with a 1 cm firm nodule on the lower leg which has been present for 8 months. She is unsure as to how this appeared. Examination showed a firm flesh-coloured nodule with no surface change which puckered on gentle squeezing of the edges. The most likely diagnosis is
explanation: The description is of a dermatofibroma which is a histiocytic lesion that often occurs on the lower legs of women and may be related to an insect bite or trauma. Nodular melanoma should always be included in the differential of a nodule on the leg as it can be amelanotic. The firm consistency and puckering on squeezing should aid in the diagnosis of a dermatofibroma.

question: Which of the following treatments is the least suitable treatment for superficial basal cell carcinoma?
explanation: Diclofenac sodium (Solaraze) gel is only licensed for the treatment of thin actinic keratoses. Although all other treatments listed can be used, the choice will depend on the site, size, thickness and overall risk of recurrence.

question: In which anatomical sites do squamous cell carcinomas ha'Je worst prognosis?
explanation: The prognosis and risk of metastasis of squamous cell carcinoma depend on several factors which include size, histology (poorly-differentiated) and past medical history (transplant patients are at particular risk). Squamous cell carcinoma arising on the ear is associated with a poor prognosis.

question: In which group of patients will staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome be associated with a poor prognosis?
explanation: Conditions associated with poor prognosis in staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome (SSSS) include diabetes and haemodialysis. Toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN) is the main differential diagnosis; however TEN involves the entire epidermis as opposed to SSSS in which the split is at the granular layer. 120 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: A 23-year old man presented with a 6-month history of slightly pr,uritic scaly hypopigmented patches on the shoulders and back which worsen following sun exposure. Examination showed hypopigmented patches with some fine scaling and no loss of hair colour within the patches. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Pityriasis versicolor is caused by the yeast Pltyrosporum orbiculare, a lipophillc yeast hence it thrives on the sebaceous-rich areas of the back. Increased temperature and humidity leads to worsening of the condition. Vitiligo presents with deplgmented patches with no epidermal change. Poliosis (loss of hair colour) is a sign in vitiligo. Idiopathic guttate hypomelanosis is an idiopathic condition In which porcelain-white small macules appear predominantly on the lower legs. Hypopigmented patches can represent rare variants of sarcoidosis and mycosis fungoides.

question: The "two-feet one hand syndrome" refers to the involvement of both feet and a single hand in
explanation: This phrase is used to describe the occurrence of tinea manum {often the dominant hand) associated with bilateral tinea pedis. The commonest cause of tinea pedis is Trichophyton rubrum followed by Trichophyton interdigitale. Psoriasis, atopic, allergic contact dermatitis as well as mycosis fungoides can all affect both the hands and feet.

question: Which of the following is the auto-antigen in dermatitis herpetiformis?
explanation: Epidermal transglutaminases is the dominant auto-antigen in dermatitis herpetiformis. Collagen VII is the target in epidermolysis bullosa acquista, whilst BP 230 and 180 are the auto-antigens in bullous pemphigoid. 121 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: Which of the following statements regarding lgA in dermatitis herpetiformis (DH) is true?

choices.A: Granular lgA deposits may also be seen in the skin of patients with epidermolysis bullosa acquisita
choices.B: lgA deposits are not seen in the skin of patients with Isolated coeliac disease
choices.C: lgA deposits are uniformly intense throughout the skin
choices.D: lgA deposits may decrease after treatment with drugs
choices.E: Linear lgA deposits in normal-appearing skin is the most reliable criterion for the diagnosis of DH

correct_text: lgA deposits are not seen in the skin of patients with Isolated coeliac disease
explanation: Granular (or fibrillar) lgA deposits in dermal papillary tips of peri-lesional and uninvolved skin of patients is a typical finding In dermatitis herpetiformis. lgA deposits have not been seen in the skin of patients with isolated coeliac disease (without dermatitis herpetiformis). lgA deposits in dermatitis herpetiformis are unaffected by treatment with drugs. lgA deposits may decrease in intensity or disappear after long-term gluten-free diet. ,., lgA deposits are not uniformly intense throughout the skin. ,., These deposits may be more easily and intensely seen in normal-appearing peri- lesional skin. ,., lgA deposits may also be seen in the skin of patients with bullous pemphigoid, Henoch Schonlein purpura, and alcoholic liver disease, although the patterns of distribution is different than those seen in dermatitis herpetiformis.

question: A 55-year old diabetic woman presents with tense serous bullae on the lower legs. There is no perilesional erythema. Which of the following statements is correct?
