choices.A: Direct immunofluoresence shows lgG and C3 at the dermo-epidermal junction
choices.E: There is a direct correlation with glycaemic control

explanation: Bullous disease of diabetes (bullosis diabeticorum) is a spontaneous, non- inflammatory, blistering condition of acral skin in patients with diabetes mellitus. The aetiology is obscure and a history of antecedent trauma is not always forthcoming. Many patients have associated nephropathy or neuropathy. Tense, non-tender blisters are seen on non-erythematous, non-urticated areas of the feet or lower legs. Other involved sites include the fingers, toes, hands, arms and rarely, non-acral sites may be involved. ,., Histology is non-specific and immunofluorescence Is negative. The blister may be in subcorneal, intraepidermal, or subepidermal location. The condition is self-limiting and the blisters heal spontaneously within 2-6 weeks of onset. 122 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: A 60-year-old woman presents with a non-tender violaceous annular plaque on the dorsum of her hand. She is taking methotrexate for rheumatoid arthritis. A skin biopsy shows palisaded granulomas associated with necrobiosis and increased deposition of dermal mucin. Which one of the following statements regarding this condition is true?

choices.B: Increasing the dose of methotrexate may Improve the skin lesions
choices.C: Spontaneous resolution can be expected in 2 years
choices.D: The disease follows severity of rheumatoid arthritis
choices.E: There is an association with rheumatoid arthritis

correct_text: Spontaneous resolution can be expected in 2 years
explanation: The clinical features and histology are typical of granuloma annulare (GA). GA most commonly affects the dorsum of hands and feet. GA can present as subcutaneous, perforating, disseminated and the rare interstitial variants. Localised forms of GA are generally not associated with systemic illnesses. Disseminated GA may be associated with diabetes mellitus. Localised GA tends to resolve spontaneously (80% clearance in 2 years). Disseminated GA lasts longer. Potent topical and intralesional corticosteroids are the treatment of choice for localised lesions. Phototherapy can be used in disseminated GA.

question: A 55-year-old patient presents with asymptomatic, firm, subcutaneous nodules on the elbow. A skin biopsy shows palisading granulomas with macrophages surrounding the eosinophilic fibrinoid degeneration of the collagen in the deep dermis. Which of the following is the most likely associated systemic disorder?
explanation: Rheumatoid nodules are most commonly seen on the elbows. Other common sites include the extensor surfaces of the fingers. Achilles tendon, ischial tuberosities and sacrum.They occur in 25%of patients with rheumatoid arthritis.

question: A 70-year old woman is admitted with chronic renal failure. She develops gangrenous areas on her thighs. A skin biopsy shows calcific deposits in blood vessels, necrosis and panniculitis. Which of the following statements is true?

choices.A: Intravenous sodium thiosulphate may bring about resolution
choices.C: Primary hyperparathyroidism is the aetiological factor
choices.D: Prognosis is excellent with spontaneous improvement in most
choices.E: Serum calcium levels are generally low

correct_text: Intravenous sodium thiosulphate may bring about resolution
explanation: Calciphylaxis or calcific uraemic arteriolopathy refers to calcification affecting small blood vessels. Secondary hyperparathyroidism results in high or normal levels of serum calcium and phosphate results in spreading skin necrosis. Purple mottling is followed by painful skin ulceration. Management includes restricting calcium and phosphate in diet and using a lower dialysate calcium concentration. Bisphosponates and intravenous infusions of sodium thiosulfate have been used successfully. 123 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: A 3-month old preterm boy is admitted with a few week history of scaling and vesicular eruption in the peri-oral and acral distribution. The child is irritable and has been having diarrhoea for 4 weeks. What is the most likely cause of these symptoms?
explanation: Acrodermatitis enteropathica may be autosomal recessive or acquired. It is caused by deficiency of zinc. Scaling and vesicles in a peri-orificial and acral distribution are common. Diarrhoea is often present. At risk population includes premature infants, aicoholics and patients with absorption defects. Zinc replacement brings about rapid improvement.

question: A 4-week old Afro-Caribbean boy presents to the dermatology clinic with pigmented macules on the trunk which followed clearance of pus-filled spots. The following statement is true

choices.C: The clinical course is protracted and may last many years
choices.D: The rash is more common in Afro-Caribbean babies

correct_text: The rash is more common in Afro-Caribbean babies
explanation: The clinical picture described above is that of transient neonatal pustular melanosis. It affects approximately 5% of black neonates and <1% of white neonates. Transient vesiculopustules which resolve in 48 hours give way to pigmented macules. The pigmented macules usually resolve within 3 months. The pustule is subcorneal and neutrophilic. Unlike erythema tox1eum neonatorum, peripheral eosinophilia is absent. The condition is self-limiting and no treatment is requiied.

question: A 14-week-old girl is referred with a 12-week history of a rapidly enlarging bruise-like swelling of the left upper eyelid completely obscuring the left eye. Examination shows a large haemangioma filling the left upper eyelid and orbit, completely closing the eye. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
explanation: Oral propranolol has replaced oral corticosteroids as the mainstay of treatment for high risk haemangiomas including those that risk loss of vision. It should also be considered for subglottic or nasal haemangiomas or rapidly enlarging haemangiomas.

question: A-12 week old boy has an enlarging tender ulcerated haemangioma on the perine::il area. Which of the following statements Is Incorrect?

choices.A: Becaplermin 0.01% gel is the mainstay treatment
choices.B: Intralesional steroids are the treatment of choice
choices.C: Potent topical corticosteroids are usually ineffective
choices.D: Pulsed dye laser is ineffective for pain control
choices.E: Spontaneous resolution is unlikely in perinea! haemangioma

correct_text: Pulsed dye laser is ineffective for pain control
explanation: Pulsed-dye laser is effective for treating ulcerated hemangiomas and can result in pain reduction, rapid re-epithelialization, and hastened involution. There is a small risk of worsening of ulceration with pulsed dye laser. Pulsed dye laser is not used routinely in the treatment of uncomplicated haemangiomas. Long pulsed and frequency-doubled Nd:YAG lasers may also be used to treat ulcerated haemangiomas. Topical imiquimod cream, becaplermin 0.01% gel and oral propranol have all been used successfully in the treatment of infantile haemangiomas. 124 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: A 3-year old boy presents with dry scaly skin since birth. Examination shows dark, polygonal, firmly adherent scales on the posterior neck, upper trunk, and extensor surfaces of the extremities. He has a history of cryptorchidism. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: X-linked ichthyosis is caused by deficiency of the enzyme steroid sulfatase (STS). The scaling is mild in the first few days of life and gives way to dark brown, polygonal, firmly adherent scales. Palms and soles are usually spared. During late childhood the rash becomes more prominent on the trunk and extremities, particularly on the extensor surfaces of the legs. Corneal opacities may be seen in patients and carriers. Cryptorchidism occurs in 20% of patients.

question: A 14-week-old girl was referred with a 12-week history of a rapidly enlarging bruise-like swelling of the left upper eyelid completely obscuring the left eye. She had repeated episodes of fresh rectal bleeding. l:xamination shows a large haemangioma filling the left upper eyelid and orbit. Computerised tomographic scan of abdomen shows a large haemangioma in the right lobe of the liver and extensive small intestinal haemangiomas. Which of the following most likely describes the condition?
explanation: PHACES syndrome is a neurocutaneous syndrome representing a spectrum of anomalies in which segmental haemangiomas, most commonly of the face, are associated with one or more of: posterior fossa brain malformations, arterial anomalies, coarctation of the aorta and cardiac defects, and eye abnormalities (PHACES if ventral developmental defects such as sternal clefting and/or supra umbilical raphe are included). The most common manifestations noted are structural and arterial anomalies of the brain, followed by cardiac anomalies and/or coarctation of the aorta, eye abnormalities, and ventral developmental defects. The most commonly reported sites for visceral haemanglomas among such patients are the brain and mediastinum. 125 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: Which of the following statements is false?

choices.A: Buccal macules in Peutz-Jeghers syndrome may disappear over time
choices.B: Buccal mucosa I macules are a pathognomonic feature of Peutz-jeghers syndrome
choices.C: Mutation in the serine/threonine kinase 11 (STKll or LKBl) gene is responsible for more than half of all cases of Peutz-Jeghers syndrome
choices.D: Pigmented macules in Peutz-Jeghers syndrome are absent at birth
choices.E: The most common malignancies associated with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome are gastrointestinal

correct_text: Buccal macules in Peutz-Jeghers syndrome may disappear over time
explanation: Peutz-Jeghers syndrome is an autosomal dominant malignant predisposition syndrome. Mucocutaneous pigmentation and intestinal hamartomatous polyposis are hallmarks of the disease. Small hyperpigmented macules appear on the lips and buccal mucosa in childhood. Pigmented lesions are not present at birth. Lip macules may disappear over time. Macules of the buccal mucosa are pathognomonic and do not tend to disappear with time. Peutz-Jeghers syndrome is associated with internal malignancies. Of the associated internal malignancies, gastrointestinal (small intestine, colorectal, stomach, pancreas) malignancies are most common. Surveillance is therefore required from an early age. Mutation in the serine/threonine kinase 11 (STK11 or LKBl) gene Is responsible for more than half of all cases of Peutz-Jeghers syndrome.

question: Which of the following is not a cause of exogenous ochronosis?
explanation: Exogenous ochronosis results from the use of certain medications, including hydroquinone, anti-malarials and products containing resorcinol, phenol, mercury, and picric acid. It presents as asymptomatic hyperpigmentation of the face, sides and back of the neck, back, and extensor sites of the extremities. Yellowish-brown globules accumulate in the papillary dermis. Unlike endogenous ochronosis, there is no articular, renal, or cardiovascular involvement. 126 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of Melkersson-Rosenthal syndrome?
explanation: Granulomatous cheilitis represents acute onset of asymmetric swelling of the upper and less commonly lower lip. Erythema, scaling, fissuring, and erosions may also develop. There is prolonged and recurrent course with eventual fixed swelling. Melkersson-Rosenthal syndrome is characterized by lingua plicata ( fissured or fur rowed tongue), facial paralysis/ptosis, and granulomatous chellltis. Granulomatous cheilitis may be the sole manifestation of this syndrome. Treatment of granulomatous cheilitis is generally unsatisfactory.

question: Which of the following is not associated with geographic tongue?
explanation: Geographic tongue is a benign inflammatory condition that affects 2% of the popul tion. It results from loss of filiform papillae. Erythematous plaques are seen with an annular or serpiginous well-demarcated white border. A changing geographic appearance is noted with time. Incidence is increased in patients with more severe or early-onset psoriasis. Treatment is not needed except in symptomatic patients in whom topical corticosteroids and analgesics may be useful. Besides psoriasis, geographic tongue is seen in Reiter s syndrome and is associated with atopic dermatitis, diabetes mellitus, anaemia, hormonal disturbances, Down s syndrome, and lithium therapy.

question: Which of the following is associated with fissured tongue?
explanation: Fissured tongue (small irregular fissures on lateral dorsal tongue) is also known as lingua plicata and may be a normal variant. It is also a classic but non-specific feature of Melkersson-Rosenthal syndrome. Other associated conditions include psoriasis, Down s syndrome, acromegaly, and Sjogren syndrome. Regular brushing of the tongue is emphasized to eliminate any associated bacterial overgrowth. 127 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: Which of the following is the aetiologic agent of oral hairy leukoplakla?
explanation: Oral hairy leukoplakia is an asymptomatic condition caused by Epstein-Barr virus. It presents as corrugated, white plaques with accentuation of the vertical folds along the lateral borders of the tongue. It occurs predominantly in immunosuppressed patients, especially HIV-infected individuals in which it is an AIDS-defining illness. It may also occur in organ transplant recipients and in patients on chemotherapy. It responds to aciclovir and cidofovir. Other anecdotal treatments include topical retinoids, and podophyllin.

question: Which of the following is not a known cause of macroglossia?
explanation: Disproportionate enlargement of the tongue relative to the jaw size is called macroglossia. It may be congenital or acquired. Pressure against the teeth results in scalloping along lhe lateral aspects of the tongue. Problems include difficulty with mastication and speech and accidental tongue biting are common. Causes include Down s syndrome, hypothyroidism, Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome, neurofibromatosis, infection by mycobacteria, filamentous bacteria, or fungus. Macroglossia caused by amyloid deposition results in woody in duration of the tongue.

question: Which of the following is not associated with periodontal disease?
explanation: Periodontal disease is associated with Human Immunodeficiency Virus, diabetes, Down s syndrome, and Langerhans cell histiocytosis. Additionally, children with Papillon-Lefevre syndrome also develop severe and destructive periodontal disease. Treatment options include oral retinoids in Papillon-Lefevre syndrome, and external beam radiation in periodontal disease of Langerhans cell hlstiocytosis. 128 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: Which of the following is not a recognized cause of gingival hyperplasia?
explanation: Causes of gingival hypertrophy include: -Leukat?mi:: hyperplasia e.g. acute myeloblastic and myelomonocytic leukaemia. -Glycogen storage disease type lb. Medications e.g. phenytoin, calcium channel blockers, and ciclosporin.

question: Which of the following is not true of cyclic neutropaenia?

choices.A: Antibiotics do not help alveolar bone loss
choices.C: Oral ulcers recur at intervals of 21-27 days
choices.E: Ulcerative gingivostomatitis is the presenting feature

correct_text: Antibiotics do not help alveolar bone loss
explanation: Cyclic neutropaenia is an autosomal dominant disorder. Acyclic decrease in the circulating neutrophils is seen. It presents with ulcerative gingivostomatitis. Oral lesions last few days and recur at 21 to 27 day intervals. Progression to periodontal disease may be seen. Alveolar bone loss may occur over time. Spontaneous improvement is seen as neutrophil counts improve. Systemic a:,tibiotic therapy m3y prevent bcne loss.

question: Which of the following is not associated with labial melanotic ma.::ules?
explanation: Multipl(; labial melanotic macules are associated with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome, Carney complex, and Laugier-Hunziker syndrome.

question: Which of the following is not associated with oral pigmentation?
explanation: Some medications may induce pigmentary changes of the oral mucosa. Women appear more susceptible. The common medications causing intra-oral pigmentary changes include minocycline, anti-malarials, clofazimine, amiodarone and zidovudine. This acquired pigmentation fades after discontinuation of the implicated medication or it may persist for months to years. 129 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: A 44-year-old woman is admitted with fever, chest and hip pains, and a recurrent non-pruritic urticaria! eruption that lasts for few hours and coincides with febri:e episodes. Haematological investigations show raised erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and C-Reactiv~ Protein (CRP) and serum lgM. A skin biopsy shows perivascular neutrophilic inflammation. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Features of Schnitzler s syndrome include chronic non-pruritic urcicaria, monoclonal lgM gammopathy, intermittent fever, asthenia, arthralgia, and bone pain with imaging evidence of osteosclerosis. Biological findings usually include an increase in white blood cell count, ESR and CRP, which reflect an inflammatory syndrome and the presence of the monoclonal lgM. Skin biopsy findings often include mononuclear or neutrophilic perivascular infiltrates. Treatment with NSAIDs, dapsone, colchicine alone is usually unsatisfactory. Recently Anaklnra, an interleukin-1 receptor antagonist has been found to be an effective treatment.

question: A-45 year old presents wi1:h widespread chronic plaque psoriasis. He also complains of joint pains. Radiological examination confirmed psoriatic arthritis. What is the commonest type of psoriatic arthritis?
explanation: Up to 30% patients with psoriasis suffer from psoriatic arthritis. IV The five types of psoriatic arthritis are: 1. Asymmetric - affects 60-70%- commonly involves fingers or toes. 2. Symmetric polyarthritis -15% - resembles rheumatoid arthritis. 3. Distal interphalengeal joint disease - 5% 4. Destructive arthritis (arthritis mutilans) - 5% 5. Axial arthritis - 5% - resembles ankylosing spondylitis.

question: A 60-year old man is admitted with an erythematous and scaly rash covering 95% of his body surface area. He is feeling cold and shivery and is noted to have generalised lymphadenopathy. What is the commonest cause of erythroderma overall?
explanation: This patient has erythroderma which by definition is involvement of >90% bod·{ surface area with an erythematous and scaly rash. The cause remains unknown in the majority of cases (30%}. Where a cause can be found, drug reactions are most commonly implicated. Pre-existing skin diseases like atopic dermatitis and psoriasis, lymphoma and contact dermatitis are other causes of erythroderma. 130 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: A 48-year old man was admitted with a 6-week history of diarrhoea and burning micturition. He also complained of red, itchy eyes and lower back pain. Examination showed erosions on the glans penis. Which organism is most commonly implicated in the pathogenesis of this condition?
explanation: Reiter s syndrome comprises of classic triad of arthritis, non-gonococcal urethritis, and conjunctivitis. It is also known as reactive arthritis and may be triggered following an enteric or urogenital infection. Symptoms appear 1-3 weeks from onset of urethritis/cervicitis or diarrhoea. It is associated with Human Leukocyte Antigen (HLA)-B27. Dermatological features incude shallow painless ulcers on the meatus and glans penis in a circinate pattern- circinate balanitis. Hyperkeratotic psoriasiform thickening of palmar/plantar skin may be seen- keratoderma blennorrhagica. Onychodystrophy and superficial oral ulcers may be present. The most commonly implicated enteric pathogen in reactive arthritis is Campylobacter. Chlamydia is the most common cause of non-gonococcal urethritis.

question: A 35-year old woman presents with erosions under her breasts and axillae. Her mother had similar symptoms which were treated as flexural psoriasis. Which of the following statements regarding this condition is incorrect?

choices.A: Direct immunofluoresence shows lgG and C3 deposition at dermo-epidermal junction
choices.B: Kaposi's varicelliform eruption is a recognised complication
choices.C: The defect is identified on ATP2C1 gene
choices.E: White bands on the fingernails may be seen

correct_text: Direct immunofluoresence shows lgG and C3 deposition at dermo-epidermal junction
explanation: Hailey-Hailey disease (familial chronic benign pemphigus) is an autosomal dominant disorder with incomplete penetrance. Approximately one thirds of patients do not have a family history of the disorder. The defect appears to be in a calcium pump protein, ATP2C1 which encodes the secretory pathway Ca2+/Mn2 ATPase (hSPCA1). Patients present with crusts and vesicles studded on erythematous plaques in flexural areas including the genital infra-mammary region, neck, and axillae. Longitudinal leukonychia may be seen on fingernails. Treatment is aimed at suppressing symptoms and includes anti-perspirants, antibacterials, topical steroids and immunosuppressives in recalcitrant cases.

question: You examine a lesion with a dermatoscope and find several maple leaf-like areas and arborising vessels. Which of the following do the above features best describe?
explanation: Other desmoplastic features of basal cell carcinoma (BCC) include blue-gray blotches, ovoid nests and globules in pigmented BCC, pink white shiny areas and spoke wheels. 131 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: A 3-year-old girl is referred to paediatric dermatology with a vascular malformation on the left side of the face. She is under the care of the neurologists for epilepsy. The condition is diagnosed as Sturge-Weber syndrome. Which of the following lasers will be most appropriate for treating this vascular deformity?
explanation: Pulsed dye laser (PDL) was the first vascular specific laser used fer the treatment of port-wine stains. It is still the gold standard for the treatment of port-wine stains. The chromophore for 585 nm and 595 nm wavelengths (PDL) is haemoglobin. The selective heating of haemoglobin by these wavelengths results in destruction of the aberrant vessels. Deeper vascular malformations may respond to the Nd:YAG laser.

question: A 70-year old woman presents with bluish-grey pigmentation on the forehead. She had been on long-term minocycline for bullous pemphigoid. She is seeking your advice on laser treatment. Which of the following lasers is likely to be effective in the treatment of her forehead pigmentation?
explanation: Minocycline pigmentation would resolve without active intervention and adequate sun protection. The Q-switched lasers (Nd:YAG, Alexandrite and Ruby) will be effective in lightening the pigmentation.

question: In which of the following conditions would you institute prophylactic antibiotics prior to dermatological surgery procedures on a contaminated wound?
explanation: Antibiotic prophylaxis for dermatologic surgery is indicated for: High risk cardiac conditions: - Prosthetic cardiac valve or prosthetic material used for valve repair. - Prior infective endocarditis. - Cardiac transplant recipients who develop valvulopathy. - Congenital heart disease. High risk prosthetic joint indications: - First 2 years post joint replacement. - lmmunosuppressed patients. - Malnourishment, malignancy, haemophilia, type 1 diabetes. Prophylaxis is not indicated for simple biopsies, curettage or excision. It is, however, indicated for procedures, especially Mohs surgery, and when reconstruction lasts >20 minutes and when the wound is contaminated or infected. 132 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: You are going to operate on a very anxious patient. All the following help to reduce pain from local anaesthetic injections except
explanation: Besides the above the following tips help to decrease pain with local anaesthetic injections: - Topical anaesthetic. - Buffer with sodium bicarbonate. - lriject slowly through a dilated pore or wound edge. - Deeper injections into subcutaneous area. - Minimal needle punctures. - Consider ring blocks.

question: Which of the following is not an amide anaesthetic?
explanation: Procaine, chloroprocaine and tetracaine are Ester anaesthetics. Lignocaine, mepivacaine, prilocaine and bupivacaine are Amide anaesthetics. Amide anaesthetics are more commonly used in skin surgery and can easily be remembered as they contain the letter I .

question: A 35-year old woman presents with ptosis of her left upper eyelid 4 days following botulinum toxin injections for forehead wrinkles. What is the best treatment?
explanation: Apraclonidine eye drops (alpha 2 adrenergic agonist) are used to reverse the ptosis induced by botulinum toxin injections.

question: A 75-year old man presents with recurrent crops of small, pruritic blisters on the scalp, face and neck. Examination shows atrophic scars and small vesicles on the scalp. There was no involvement of oral mucosa. A punch biopsy shows a non- inflammatory, subepidermal blister and direct immunofluoresence demonstrates linear deposits of complement C3 and lgG at the dermo-epidermal junction. What is the diagnosis?
explanation: Brunsting-Perry cicatritial pemphigoid is a rare variant of cicatritial pemphigoid. It is most commonly seen in elderly males. Clinical features include pruritic, recurrent crops of vesicles which heal with atrophic scars. The vesicles are confined mainly to the head and neck. Histopathology shows subepidermal blisters with prominent perivascular infiltrates of lymphocytes, polymorphonuclears, eosinophils and prominent fibrosis in late stages. Direct immunofluoresence shows staining with lgG and C3. Successful treatments include dapsone and sulphamethoxypyridazine. 133 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: Which of the following is not a poor prognostic factor in cutaneou5 squamous cell carcinoma {SCC)?
explanation: Factors determining poor prognosis in cutaneous SCC include tumour size > 2 cm, tumour depth> 2 mm (especially> 6 mm), tumour at sites of radiation, thermal damage, ulceration, sinuses, inflammation, scars or Bowen s disease, non-exposed sites, ear, and lip. Spindle cell (carcinosarcomas), acantholytic, desmoplastic histological subsets. Histological features of aggression including perineural or perivascular involvement, or both, Broders grades 3 and 4, host immunosuppression and recurrent lesions, lymph-node involvement or distant metastasis.

question: A 70-year old man presents with a biopsy-proven basal cell carcinoma (BCC) on his forehead. He had this lesion treated with radiotherapy nearly 4 years ago. Which of the following is contra-indicated for the treatment of this lesion?
explanation: Side-effects of radiotherapy include dyspigmentation, telangiectasia, and radiodystrophy, resulting in a poor cosmetic outcome. Radiotherapy is contra-indicated in the treatment of BCCs that have recurred after radiotherapy.

question: A 68-year old patient has superficial basal cell carcinomas (sBCCs) on the upper chest. The dermatologist has prescribed a cream which acts by stimulating toll-like receptor 7. The active ingredient in the cream is
explanation: lmiquimod is a synthetic immune-response modifier belonging to the imidazoqulnolone family. It acts by stimulating toll-like receptor 7, which is expressed on dendritic ceils and monocytes, leading to increased production of cytokines and chemokines, which in turn promote both T-helper-1 innate and adaptive cell-mediated immune responses. Topical 5% imiquimcd cream is an emerging non-invasive therapeutic option for sBCCs. Local skin reactions including erythema, oedema, pruritus, erosion, ulceration, dyspigmentation, and scabbing are common side-effects. 134 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: Which of the following statements regarding photodynamic therapy is false?

choices.A: Photodynamic therapy is associated with a better cosmetic outcome than cyrotherapy in the treatment of superficial basal cell carcinoma {sBCC)
choices.B: Photodynamic therapy is recommended for the treatment of small squamous cell carcinomas (SCCs)
choices.C: Surgical excision is more effective than photodynamic therapy for treatment of nodular basal cell carcinoma (nBCCs)
choices.D: Topical methylaminolevulinate and 5-aminolevulinic acid photodynamic therapy are effective treatments for sBCCs
choices.E: Topical methylaminolevulinate and 5-aminolevulinic acid photodynamic therapy are equally effective in the treatment of small nBCCs

correct_text: Photodynamic therapy is recommended for the treatment of small squamous cell carcinomas (SCCs)
explanation: Topical methyl aminolevulinate and 5-aminolevulinic acid photodynamic therapy are effer.tive treatments for sBCCs. Results of a study directly comparing these two photosensitisers in treatment of nBCCs showed no difference In efficacy. Surgical excision is more effective than fractionated illuminated 5-aminolevulinic acid photodynamic therapy for treatment of nBCCs. For patients with sBCCs, methyl-aminolevulinate photodynamic therapy has a similar response to that of cryosurgery but cosmetic outcome is better with photodynamic therapy. Since data are scarce for the efficacy of topical photodynamic therapy in primary cutaneous invasive SCCs, topical therapy cannot be recommended for SCC.

question: Whilst reading a histopathology report you come across the term Breslow thickness. You are aware that this determines the prognosis in cutaneous melanoma. Breslow thickness Is measured from
explanation: Breslow tumour thickness is measured from the top of the granular layer or the base of an ulcer to the deepest point of tumour invasion using an optical micrometer. As a general rule the thicker the Breslow thickness, the poorer the prognosis.

question: A 70-yearold man is admitted with weight loss and fatigue. He is noted to have ichthyosis. A computed tomography scan showed mediastinal lymphadenopathy. You make a diagnosis of acquired ichthyosis. Which of the following is not a recognised cause of acquired ichthyosis?
explanation: Acquired ichthyosis is associated with malignancies (especially Hodgkin s lymphoma), non-Hodgkin lymphoma, mycosis fungoides, myeloma, Kaposi s sarcoma, leiomyosr1rcoma, and carcinomas of the lung, breast, ovary, and cervix. ,., Sarcoidosis, leprosy, thyroid disease, hyperparathyroidism, nutritional disorders, chronic renal failure, bone marrow transplantation, and HIV infection can all cause ichthyosis. Auto-immune diseases, including systemic lupus erythematosus and dermatomyositis. Medications - nicotinic acid, triparanol, butyrophenones, dixyrazine, cimetidine, and clofazimine.

question: A 58-year old man underwent excision of a yellow nodule on the upper eyelid that is histologically confirmed as sebaceous adenoma. He has a family history of colonic carcinoma. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Muir-Torre syndrome refers to the presence of sebaceous adenoma, sebaceoma, or sebaceous carcinoma with visceral cancer, usually gastrointestinal or genito-urinary. Patients may also present with other cutaneous lesions including keratoacanthoma, squamous cell carcinoma, or multiple follicular cysts. 135 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: Which of the following best represent corps rands in Darier's disease?
explanation: Histological features of Darter s disease include: - Hyperkeratosis. - Focal dyskeratosis (premature, abnormal keratinisation of keratinocytes). - Eosinophilic dyskeratotic cells - corps rands in the stratum spinosum, grains in the upper layers of the epidermis. - Corps ronds and grains correspond to apoptotic keratinocytes. - Suprabasal acantholysis and clefts. - Electron microscopy shows separation of the keratin filaments from the desmosomes and clumping of perinuclear tonofilaments.

question: Which of the following is a key component of inner dense plaque?
explanation: Desmosomal proteins fall into three major gene families: - Plakins -desmoplakin. - Armadillo proteins-plakoglobin and plakophilins. - Desmosomal cadherins- desmogleins and desmocollins. Plakins and armadillo proteins are found in the plaque. Desmosomal cadherins are extracellular amino-termini of transmembrane proteins, which comprise the desmogleins. Desmoplakin is the major inner plaque component.

question: Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding auto-inflammatory syndromes?

choices.A: Abdominal pain is common in acute attacks
choices.C: Fever is often present in acute attacks
choices.D: Raised inflammatory markers are almost always seen in acute attacks
choices.E: The predominant skin eruption during acute attacks consists of a maculopapular exanthem

correct_text: The predominant skin eruption during acute attacks consists of a maculopapular exanthem
explanation: Auto-inflammatory syndromes are characterised by the presence of fever, abdominal pain, arthralgia and an urticaria! eruption during acute attacks. Raised inflammatory markers are almost always found during acute attacks. Its absence almost always excludes the presence of an auto-Inflammatory syndrome. These syndromes represent dysfunction of the innate immunity (neutrophils and macrophages) in the absence of auto-antibodies. Examples of auto-inflammatory syndromes include hyper lgD syndrome, Schnitzler s syndrome, cryopyrin-associated-periodic-fever syndrome, TNF-receptor-associated periodic fever-syndrome (TRAPS) and familial Mediterranean fever. 136 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: Which of the following drugs is most likely to cause systemic vasculitis due to the induction of p-ANCA?
explanation: All the above listed drugs can result in positive p-ANCA with or without systemic vasculitis. Propylthiouracil is an anti-thyroid drug most commonly associated with the induction of systemic vasculitis through p-ANCA which can occur several months to years following initiation of therapy. Other causes of positive p-ANCA Include Inflammatory bowel disease, rheumatoid arthritis and tuberculosis.

question: Which of the following is the most important prognostic factor in the diagnosis of melanoma?
explanation: The thickness, measured as Breslow thickness, is the most important prognostic factor in melanoma. All other factors are also important but the survival rate strongly correlates with the thickness of the tumour.

question: CD56 is a marker for which of the following cells?
explanation: CD56 is a helpful marker in the diagnosis of natural killer cells. S100 and Melan-A are markers for melanocytes. CD68 is a marker for macrophages. CD20 and CD79a are markers for B-cells. CD2, CD3, CD4, CDS, CD7 and CD8 are all markers ofT-cells.

question: A 12-year-old Pakistani girl was referred with a long-standing history of general stiffening of the tongue with the presence of beaded papules on the eyelids and on the perl-orbital skin and hoarseness of her voice. There are also verrucous- like plaques on the elbows and knuckles, in addition to dental anomalies. Further history reveals that her older sister, aged 16, suffers from the same condition. The inheritance pattern of this condition is?

choices.A: An acquired condition therefore not inherited

explanation: The diagnosis here is lipoid proteinosis which is a rare autosomal recessive disorder characterised by the above signs and symptoms. It is caused by a mutation of the gene ECN-1. 137 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: A 65-year-old man presents with photo-distributed eczema that is worse each time he works in his garden. You therefore suspect allergic contact dermatitis and perform patch testing to series which include chemicals and plants. Which of the following chemicals is found predominantly In wood?
explanation: Dalbergiones are chemicals found mainly in wood and should therefore be suspected in wood cutters. Tulpulin-A is the main allergen found in Tulips. Primin is the main allergen in the Primula plant. Sesquiterpene lactone mix is an allergen found in many plants and therefore can serve in many cases as a screening for possible plant allergy. Other chemicals that can be found in plants or trees include oak, moss, terpenes and propolis.

question: A 46-year-old woman has been complaining of intractable vulval dermatitis for the last five years for which she has tried several prescribed and over-the- counter preparations, some of which aggravates her dermatitis. You suspect allergic contact dermatitis and therefore advise patch testing. Which of the following allergens is least likely to be relevant in this case?
explanation: Nickel Sulphate is the most commonly found allergen including in patients who have been patched for vulva I contact dermatitis however, it is the least likely to be relevant in this situation. Vulval contact dermatitis is often caused by preservatives, topical anaesthetics, perfumes, neomycin and patients own products. More recently, in the United Kingdom, positive patch test reactions to sodium metabisulphite, as in trimovate., cream, have been increasingly seen in this condi .ion.

question: Peri-orbital oedema is most likely to occur in which of the following conditions?
explanation: Other causes of peri-orbital oedema include allergic contact dermatitis to cosmetics or PPD with or without overt scalp dermatitis, dermatomyositis, angio-oedema, erysipelas, nephrotic syndrome and hypothyroidism.

question: Which of the following is least likely to result in generalized pustular psoriasis?
explanation: Generalized pustular psoriasis is a dermatological emergency in which patients are often very unwell. Leukocytosis and fever may be present. Ultraviolet-A radiation, withdrawal of steroid therapy, crude coal tar and pregnancy can all trigger generalized pustular psoriasis. It is worth checking calcium levels in pustular psoriasis as hypocalcaemia may result in therapy resistance. 138 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: Sebaceous glands are absent in which of the following?
explanation: Palms and soles do not contain sebaceous glands or hair follicles. Facial skin and in particular the nose contain the largest number of sebaceous glands.

question: Which of the following statements is correct?

choices.A: Both heparin and warfarin-induced skin necrosis are related to the production of specific antibodies against the drugs
choices.B: Heparin-induced skin necrosis is related to a drop in protein C leve;s
choices.C: Heparin-induced skin necrosis is related to the production of antibodies and therefore should never be re-challenged
choices.D: Warfarin -induced skin necrosis is related to the production of antibodies and therefore should never be re-challenged
choices.E: Warfarin-induced skin necrosis is a late manifestation of warfarin therapy, often occurring after the first six weeks

correct_text: Heparin-induced skin necrosis is related to the production of antibodies and therefore should never be re-challenged
explanation: Warfarin-induced skin necrosis often occurs between day three and eight following initiation of warfarin due to the transient pro-coagulant state secondary to a drop in protein(s) C and S levels. Heparin-induced skin necrosis occurs due to the production of antibodies and should therefore never be re-challenged with heparin, unlike warfarin which can be re-challenged provided there is concomitant use of low molecular weight heparin in the initial phase.

question: A 2-month-old boy presented with targetoid large erythematous macules with purpura and oedema on his limbs and face. History reveals that the baby suffered an upper respiratory tract infection ten days prior to the appearance of this rash. Which of the following statements regarding this condition is true?

choices.A: ANCA level must be checked immediately
choices.B: Histology will show leukocytoclastic vasculitis and the condition will resolve spontaneously
choices.C: Histology will show multiple thrombi in the superficial vessels
choices.D: The condition has a very poor prognosis and rapid initiation of corticosteroid therapy is required
choices.E: Treatment with hyperoaric oxygen is required

correct_text: Histology will show leukocytoclastic vasculitis and the condition will resolve spontaneously
explanation: Acute haemorrhagic oedema of infancy can occur following upper respiratory tract infection and clinically presents with targetoid-like purpuric macules associated with oedema. The condition is transient, has an excellent prognosis and no treatment is required other than supportive measures. Histologically, the lesions show small vessel leukocytoclastic vasculitis and occasionally lgA deposition in the vessels.

question: A 60-year-old man presented with a relatively rapid onset of an erythematous-to-orange coloured eruption, which started Initially on his face. It spread distally to involve most of his skin with some islands of normal skin on his trunk and limbs. His palms and soles have a shiny orange hue and subungual hyperkeratosis was noted. There is no personal or family history of psoriasis nor is there any joint involvement. What is the likely histological picture?

choices.B: Dense infiltrate of plasma cells extending deep into the reticular dermis
choices.C: Parakeratosis alternating with orthokeratosls in both the horizontal and vertical plains
choices.E: Wedge-shaped hypergranulosis and the presence of dyskeratotic cells

correct_text: Parakeratosis alternating with orthokeratosls in both the horizontal and vertical plains
explanation: The clinical history here is of pityriasis rubra pllaris. Histologically, this is characterised by alternating parakeratosis in the vertical and horizontal plains. The main differential is psoriasis although the presence of islands of normal skin and the orange discolouration of the palms and soles favour the diagnosis of pityriasis rubra pilaris. 139 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: Which of the following human papillomavirus serotype is not associated with epidermodysplasia verruciformis?
explanation: Epidermodysplasla verruciformis present clinically as plain pink to skin-coloured flat papules similar to plain warts. Epidermodysplasia verruciformis is associated with serotypes 3, 5, 8 and 12. HPV-16 and 18 are associated with Bowen s disease, Bowenoid papulosis and cervical cancer. Histologically, epidermodysplasia verruciformis is characterised by pale keratinocytes in the upper part of the epidermis.

question: A 12-year-old girl presents with a persistent eczematous eruption covering her face, trunk and limbs which is associated with coarse facial features, doughy skin and broad nasal bridge. She also has a history of recurrent fractures and poor dentition. She has been found to have persistently raised eosinophil count, significantly raised lgE levels but no demonstrable specific lgEs against any particular allergen. On examination, you also note that she has a high-arched palate. Mutation of which gene is responsible for this condition?
explanation: The clinical features and lab abnormalities here are consistent with the diagnosis of hyper-lgE syndrome. The autosomal dominant variant is related to STAT3 defects; however the autosomal recessive variant Is related to 1YK2 defects. Other features of this disease are recurrent pyogenic infections, asthma, hyper- extensible joints, scoliosis and neurological complications.

question: Which of the following structural hair abnormalities can be seen In Netherton's syndrome?
explanation: Trichorrhexis invaginata is also called bamboo hair and is found in Netherton s syndrome. Increased fragility of the hair shaft is also seen in monilethrix, trichorrhexis nodosa, trlchothiodystrophy and pill torti. In loose anagen syndrome and woolly hair, the hair shafts are not fragile.

question: 5-alpha-reductase is responsible for which type of hair loss?
explanation: 5-alpha-reductase converts testosterone to the more potent dihydrotestosterone which is responsible for hair loss in androgenetic alopecia. Finasteride is a drug that blocks this e11Lyme; hence it can be used in male pattern alopecia. Thyroid disease and iron deficiency anaemia can contribute to diffuse hair loss in a non-scarring fashion such as telogen effluvium. 140 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: Which of the following statements regarding the diagnosis of hidradenitis suppurativa is incorrect?

choices.B: Arthritis can be a manifestation in severe cases
choices.C: Obesity tends to worsen the condition
choices.D: Smoking tends to worsen the condition
choices.E: There is increased risk of basal cell carcinoma

correct_text: There is increased risk of basal cell carcinoma
explanation: There is increased risk of squamot•s cell carcinoma in patients with hidradenitis suppurativa due to the chronic inflammation. Lymphoedema is also a complication of the disease. Lithium tends to exacerbate hidradenitis suppurat:iva. The condition can be associated with inflammatory bowel disease, pyoderma gangrenosum, spondylo rthropathy and SAPHO syndrome.

question: Antibodies are most likely to be formed against which of the following drugs?
explanation: Infliximab is a chimeric monoclonal antibody and therefore there is a high risk of developing antibodies against it in a proportion of patients. Reduced efficacy can result due to the neutralising antibodies. Antibodies can also be produced against adalimumab but to a lesser extent than Infliximab. ,., Methotrexate can be combined with infliximab in cases where there is antibody production leading to loss of efficacy.

question: which of the following sub-types of morphea Is the commonest in children?
explanation: Linear mcrphea can be associated with joint symptoms and is the commonest subtype in children. The plaque type of morphea is the commonest in adults. En coup de Sabre sub-type of morphea on the head can be associated with ocular and neurological abnormalities.

question: Naso-septa I perforation can be found in all of the following except?
explanation: Bevacizumab is a humanised monoclonal anti- angiogenic antibody used in the treatment for various cancers. Cocaine use, Wegener s granulomatosis, trauma and bevacizumab have all been associated with naso-septal perforation. 141 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: The commonest site for intra-oral squamous cell carcinoma is?
explanation: Squamous cell carcinoma is the commonest type of oral carcinoma and is most commonly found in the floor of the mouth. Squamous cell carcinoma is more common amongst smokers and can arise from a pre-existing plaque of leukoplakia, particularly the verrucous form. Squamous cell carcinoma can arise on the lips, particularly in smokers and patients with actinic damage.

question: Parakeratosis is not a feature of which of the following?
explanation: Classic lichen planus is characterised by its absence of parakeratosis and eosinophils. Parakeratosis can be found in all of the other listecJ conditions. Eosinophils in the context of a licilenoid infiltrate should raise the suspicion of a drug aetiology.

question: Which of the following Is not a treatment option In pruritus secondary to end-stage renal failure?
explanation: Pruritus is a common feature of end-stage renal disease and treatment depend on the severity. Treatments include topical anti-pruritic therapy, UVB phototherapy, gabapentin and the use of selective neuro-epinephrine re-uptake inhibitors such as mi1tazapine. Rifampicin is used in pruritus secondary to chronic liver disease as it induces liver enzymes. Other treatments for chronic liver disease include the use of mirtazapine or paroxetine, bile acid resins and naltrexone.

question: Based on available evidence, which of the following is considered the best option for treating morphea?
explanation: Methotrexate has the best evidence and should be the first-line treatment of choice in cases of generalized or accelerated morphea. It can be combined with rnE:thyl prednisolone or precinisolone; the combination has been shown to be very effective in cases of accelerated morphea. Topical steroids, tacrolimus ointment or phototherapy can be used for localised morphea. 142 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: Which of the following is the most common manifestation of ocular rosacea?
explanation: Rosacea has four sub-types - erythematotelangiectatic, papulo-pustular, phymatous and ocular rosacea. Ocular rosacea can be found in half of the patients, which is more frequently associated with the papulo-pustular variant. Meibomian gland dysfunction is the commonest manifestation of ocular rosacea leading to dry eyes.

question: The combination of ciclosporin and statin therapy leads to increased levels oi statin which in turn can lead to statin-induced myopathy. Which of the following statins is however safe to combine with ciclosporin due to a different metabolic pathway?
explanation: This is an important reaction that dermatologists should be aware of as ciclosporin is metabolised through the CYP3A4 pathway. Most statins, with the exception of pravastatin, are metabolised through the same metabolic pathway. Hence, this is the only statin that can be safely combined with ciclosporin.

question: Which type of cryoglobulinaemia is least likely to be associated with small ve.;- sel vasculitis?
explanation: Type-1 cryoglobulinaemia is often associated with monoclonal gammopathy and occlusion of small blood vessels but rarely small vessel vasculitis. Cryoglobulinaemia types-2 and 3 are called essential mixed cryoglobulinaemia and can be associated with hepatitis C and other infections. It can be associated with small vessel vasculitis. Type-2 cryoglobulinaemia can in some cases be associated with monoclonal gammopathy.

question: Which of the following nerves is not a branch of the trigeminal nerve?
explanation: Marginal mandibular is a branch of the facial nerve, which is a motor nerve. The trigeminal nerve is a sensory nerve. All the above branches of the trigeminal nerve supply the eyelids and skin around the eyes. 143 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: Which of the following is the most common site for sebaceous carcinoma?
explanation: Sebaceous carcinoma is a rare malignancy that typically affects the eyelids. Around 25% of the cases can be extra-ocular. Sebaceous carcinoma is the fourth most common eyelid malignancy after basal cell carcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma and melanoma. Sebaceous carcinomas can metastasise and these tumours should be treated adequately through surgical excision. The presence of sebaceous carcinoma (in addition to sebaceoma and/or sebaceous adenoma) raises a suspicion of the presence of Muir-Torre syndrome.

question: A 52-year-old woman presented with a 3-year history of multiple painful and tender nodular lesions involving the upper aspects of her arms and thighs, which were followed by atrophic scarring of the affected areas. She also suffered from chronic arthralgia and myalgia. She had positive ANA and weak double- stranded DNA antibodies. A biopsy showed evidence of atrophic epidermis with peri-vascular lymphocytic infiltrate, lobular panniculitis with a lymphocytic infiltrate. The most likely diagnosis is?
explanation: Lupus profundus Is also known as lupus panniculltis, which is a chronic relapsing pannicullitis that occurs in 1 - 3% of patients with cutaneous lupus erythematosus, affecting mostly women. M Clinically, this can present with tender subcutaneous nodules and plaques with a predilection for the upper aspects of arms, shoulders and buttocks. Histologically, it affects the cutaneous fat in a lobular fashion. Treatment is with systemic steroids, hydroxychloroquine, dapsone, azathioprine or thalidomide. Systemic retinoids are often unhelpful in this condition. Erythema nodosum affects mostly the shins. Histologically, this is characterised by a septal panniculitis. Lupus pernio is a term used for a variant of cutaneous sarcoldosls affecting the nose or ears resembling a frost bite.

question: Sarcoidal granulomas can be seen in all of the following except?
explanation: Sarcoidal granulomas are so-called naked granulomas, which are characterised by the absence of necrosis. Sarcoidal granulomas can be seen in Melkerson-Rosenthal syndrome and foreign body reaction to silica, beryllium and tattoo granulomas. Granuloma annulare is characterised histologically by necrobiotic granulomas, which may also be seen in necrobiosis lipoidica, rheumatoid nodule and necrobiotic xanthogranuloma. 144 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: Epidermal desmosomes serve to adhere the cells together due to the presence of various glycoproteins. Which of the following components of the desmosomes is not targeted in paraneoplastic pemphigus?
explanation: Corneodesmosin is targeted by the autosomal dominant rare condition hypotrichosis simplex of the scalp. Plakoglobin is also targeted in the inherited disorder of Naxos disease. Desmoglein-1 is targeted in pemphigus foliaceous, whereas desmoglein 3 (and desmoglein-1) are targeted in pemphigus vulgaris. A rare variant of pemphigus called lgA-pemphigus results from antibodies targeting desmocollins.

question: A 62-year old man who Is seriously ill in intensive care with neutropaenia on a background of chronic myeloid leukaemia developed several erythematous and purpuric macules on his thigh and lower back, which rapidly developed into haemorrhagic bullae which ruptured leaving ulcers with eschars. There was a surrounding erythematous violaceous necrotic area of skin. Blood cultures will most likely show which of the following organisms?
explanation: Ecthyma gangrenosum is often a manifestation of sepsis secondary to pseudomonas aeruginosa. Predisposing causes include neutropaenia, haematological malignancies, immunodeficiency syndromes, chemotherapy, burns and Indwelling catheters. The main differential diagnosis is of pyoderma gangrenosum which is not associated with septicaemia. In rare cases, ecthyma gangrenosum can be caused by other organisms such as escherichia coli and neisseria meningitidis.

question: Frusemide is a loop diuretic that is widely used. Which of the following blistering disorders can be caused by this drug?
explanation: Va neomycin is the commonest cause of linear lgA disease. Penicillamine and ACE inhibitors are common causes of drug-induced pemphigus. Pseudo-porphyria can also be caused by thiazide diuretics and non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs.

question: All of the following conditions can increase the risk of developing basal cell carcinomas in children except
explanation: There is an increased risk for the development of melanoma arising from giant congenital naevi and not basal cell carcinomas. All other conditions have an increased risk of developing basal cell carcinomas. The commonest benign tumour which arises from the naevus sebaceous is syringocystoadenoma papilliferum. Patients with Gorlin s syndrome are known to develop multiple basal cell carcinomas from an early age. Patients with xeroderma pigmentosum are at increased risk of developing skin cancers including squamous cell carcinoma and melanoma. 145 Section 1: Answers &. Comments

question: Which of the following chemicals is not a preservative?
explanation: Mercaptobenzothiazole is a rubber allergen. It should therefore be suspected in cases where there is a suspicion of rubber allergy such as the use of gloves or In suspected shoe dematitis. ,., Other rubber allergens include carba and thiuram mix. Other preservatives include the isothiozilinones, gluteraldehyde and all the formaldehyde releasers.

question: A 65-year-old Caucasian man, who works for an international company recently returned from a foreign trip where he was working for six months. He recalled being bitten by an insect on his right cheek and gradually developed a small papule which has become ulcerated. You suspect cutaneous leishmaniasis and have taken a biopsy for both histology and culture. Which of the following leishmaniasis species causes visceral leishmanisis only with no cutaneous lesions?
explanation: Leishmaniasis donovani is the only leishmaniasis species that causes visceral leishmaniasis and typically presents with pancytopenia and splenomegaly due to involvement of both the spleen and bone marrow. All other leishmaniasis species give cutaneous lesions that are divided into new and old world cutaneous leishmaniasis, Old world cutaneous leishmaniasis is due to L.tropica, L.major, L.ethiopica and L.infantum. New world leishmaniasis is due to L.brasiliensis and L.mexicana. L.brasiliensis can result in mucosal involvement.

question: When differentiating between granuloma annulare and necrobiosis lipoidica histologically, which of the following statements is correct?

choices.A: Abundant plasma cells may be seen in granuloma annulare
choices.B: Abundant plasma cells may be seen in necrobiosis lipoidica
choices.C: Necrobiosis lipoidica often has increased mucin deposition in the dermis
choices.D: Subcutaneous involvement is only a feature found in granuloma annulare
choices.E: The type of granuloma in granuloma annulare is sarcoidal

correct_text: Abundant plasma cells may be seen in necrobiosis lipoidica
explanation: Necrobiosis lipoidica can be differentiated from granuloma annulare by the abundance of plasma cells, sclerosis and the absence of mucin. Whilst some cases of granuloma annulare can extend deep into the subcutis it is typically more superficial than necrobiosis lipoidica and subcutaneous involvement is generally not a feature. Both granuloma annulare and necrobiosis lipoidica are necrobiotic granulomas.

question: Which of the following drugs is an absolute contra-indication in patients with active hepatitis B?
explanation: The use of immunosuppressive therapy should be avoided in patients with active hepatitis Band advice from the hepatologist should be sought. ,., Ciclosporin is an absolute contra-indication in active hepatitis B. ,., Anti-TNF therapy can be used provided that adequate anti-viral therapy has been established. 146 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: You patch test a 36-year-old lady who gave a history of worsening of her eczema with the use of certain topical preparations and you found a strong positive reaction to benzalkonium chloride. Which of the following topical preparations is safe to use?
explanation: Benzalkon!um chloride is an anti-microbial chemical added in many preparations of emollients and antiseptics. Oilatum plus contains benzalkonium chloride however, all other products of oilatum do not contain this chemical.

question: Which of the following markers is a sensitive marker for mcrkel cell carcinoma?
explanation: Merkel cell carcinoma is a rare neuro-endocrine cutaneous malignancy that may arise in transplant patients. Recent!y a virus has been implicated as a possible factor in the development of merkel cell carcinoma called polyoma virus. CK20 is a very sensitive marker for merkel cell carcinoma. CD34 and Factor Xllla are helpful to distinguish between dermatofibroma and dematofibrosarcoma protuberans. CDla and S100 are helpful to differentiate between Langerhan s cells and melanocytes.

question: Which of the following conditions is not an acantholytic disorder?
explanation: Bullous pemphigoid is a blistering disease which is subepidermal and acantholysis does not take place. Hailey-Hailey and Darier s diseases are both inherited forms of acantholytic disorders. Grover s disease is also known as transient acantholytic dematosis and often presents with discrete pruritic papules and vesicles often on the back of middle aged or elderly people.

question: Which of the following statements regarding poison ivy is correct?

choices.A: Poison ivy sensitive individuals can develop peri-oral dermatitis from eating bananas
choices.B: Rubber gloves are safe to use in sensitized individuals when in contact with the plant
choices.C: The allergen responsible following contact with the plant Is urushiol
choices.D: The allergen responsible for the dermatitis following contact with the plant is primin
choices.E: The highest rate of sensitization is found in South East Asia

correct_text: The allergen responsible following contact with the plant Is urushiol
explanation: Primin is the allergen found in the primula plant. Peri-oral dermatitis to mangoes may occur in sensitized individuals. Banana can cross react with latex. The highest rate of sensitization to urushiol (responsible for poison ivy) is in North America. Urushiol is soluble in rubber and therefore vinyl gloves should be worn for protection. 147 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: Which of the followi11g statements regarding cat scratch disease is incorrect?

choices.A: Bartonellosis is the disseminated form of the infection in the immunocompromised host
choices.B: Bacillary angiomatosis is the cutaneous-limited manifestation of Bartonella henselae
choices.C: Lymphadenopathy may occur in half of the cases
choices.D: The condition is self-limiting in immunocompetents and therefore conservative management Is appropriate
choices.E: The responsible organism is Bartonella henselae

correct_text: Lymphadenopathy may occur in half of the cases
explanation: Lymphadenopathy is found in 100% of cases of cat sc.ratch disease. The condition is common in children and presents with a papulo-pustular eruption with scratch marks, mostly on the hands. Azithromycin has been used in some cases but no treatment is required in immunocompetent individuals.

question: A 53-year-old man developed an intensely pruritic eruption consisting of violaceous pa pules on his trunk and limbs with some follicular accentuation. He received a bone-marrow transplant four months prior to the onset of the eruption. Which of the following statements regarding this condition is incorrect?

choices.A: A lichenoid drug eruption is the differential diagnosis in this case
choices.B: In grade 4 of the disease the histological appearances can resemble those of toxic epidermal necrolysis
choices.C: The chronic variant always follows on from the acute setting
choices.D: The condition is primarily mediated by T lymphocyt>?s
choices.E: The incidence is highest in the setting of bone marrow transplantation

correct_text: The chronic variant always follows on from the acute setting
explanation: Chronic graft-versus-host-disease generally develops 3 months after transplantation and many not occur after the acute variant of the disease. The condition is most likely to develop in the setting of allogeneic, unmatched and unrelated donor. The 2 variants of the chronic form include lichenoid and sclerodermoid. Advanced age, male gender and the presence of HLA-DR4 allele In the recipient are all risk factors for the development of the condition.

question: A 64-year-old man with 3-year history of dermatomyositis presented with firm, painful nodules on his abdomen and limbs. Histology showed evidence of calcification in the dermis. The most likely mechanism here is
explanation: Pathologic calcification of cutaneous tissue can be dystrophic, metastatic or idiopathic. ,._ Dystrophic calcinosis cutis consists of deposition of calcium salts in abnormal or damaged tissue, mostly elastic fibres, and occurs in the setting of normal serum calcium levels particularly in connectve ti sue disorders. Metastatic calcinosis cutis occurs in the setting of hypercalcaemia and involves the calcification of normal tissues. Idiopathic calcinosis cu·::is consists of calcification of normal tissues in the setting of normal calcium levels. N Primary osteoma cutis can occur in the setting of Albright s hereditary osteodystrophy, fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva and progressive osseous heteroplasia. Secondary osteoma cutis may occur following previous dermatoses such as military osteoma cutis on the face secondary to acne vulgaris. 148 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: A 40-year-old woman recently diagnosed with acute myeloid leukaemia presented 3 weeks following treatment with the chemotherapy agent cytarabine. Clinically she had pruritic and tender papules on her forearms and chest with bilateral palmar erythema. The papules were slightly oedematous and some have coalesced to form plaques. A biopsy taken from one of the papules showed a dense neutrophilic infiltrate around eccrine glands with associated necrosis. Which of the following statements regarding this condition is incorrect?

choices.A: Acute myeloid leukaemia is the most common associated malignancy with this condition
choices.B: Cytarabine is the commonest reported chemotherapy agent responsible for this condition
choices.C: The condition is associated with a high mortality rate and future chemotherapy should be avoided
choices.D: The condition is self-limiting and treatment is often not required
choices.E: The condition usually begins within 3 weeks following chemotherapy

correct_text: The condition is associated with a high mortality rate and future chemotherapy should be avoided
explanation: Neutrophilic eccrine hidradenitis is a self-limiting condition occurring mostly within 3 weeks of cytarabine in the treatment of acute myeloid leukaemia. Other chemotherapy agents that have been reported to cause the condition include bleomycin, cycloohosphamide and doxorubicin. Systemic steroids and dapsone have been used in cases where the lesions are very painful and oedematous. Dapsone has been reported to be used successfully as prophylactic therapy.

question: Which of the following tattoo pigments should be avoided in a patient with a known contact allergy to cement?
explanation: Chromium and cobalt are both present in cement. Red tattoos can contain mercury, ferric hydrate and/or oxide. Manganese is an inorganic: salt often found In purple tattoos.

question: Which of the following delayed reactions to tattoos is the commonest?
explanation: Reactions to tattoos can either be acute or delayed. The majority of allergic contact dermatitis is related to red tattoos. Red tattoos are either due to inorganic salts of metals such as mercury or cinnabar; or due to organic preparations such as sandalwood and brazilwood. Patch testing will only be positive to the inorganic salts (i.e. mercury) and not to the organic salts due to the water insolubility of the latter. Mercury pigment is also responsible for the delayed lichenoid reactions to tattoos but patch te£ting will be negative and the clinical and histological appearances will differ from those of allergic contact dermatitis. In pseudolymphomas the lymphocytes are polyclonal as opposed to monoclonal in cutaneous lymphomas. 149 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: In which of the following subtypes of vasculitis is the presence of granulomas a feature?
explanation: Granulomas are also present in Wegener s granulomatosis but in Churg-Strauss there is often tissue eosinophilia as well. In erythema elevatum diutinum the infiltrate Is predominantly neutrophilic with areas of fibrosis (in chronic case). In granuloma faciale there are no granulomas but a Grenz zone is present separating the dermis from the epidermis. In cryoglobulinaemia a homogenous eosinophilic material is found within blood vessels.

question: Spongios!s is least likely to be present in
explanation: Although mild spongiosis can sometimes be found in cutaneous T cell lymphoma, this is absent in cutaneous B cell lymphomas. Other causes of spongiosis include pigmented purpuric dermatosis, erythroderma, Zoon s balanitis, insect bites and the pre-bullous stage of lmmunobullous disorders.

question: CD30 positivity can be seen in all of the following except
explanation: Other causes of CD30 positivity include chronic tick bites and Sezary syndrome. In marginal zone B cell lymphoma the infiltrate is positive for CD20, CD79a and bcl-2; and is negative for bcl-6 (positive in follicle centre B cell lymphoma).

question: A 36-year old man has had a changing mole on his back removed. This was reported histologically to be a superficial spreading melanoma, Breslow thickness of 3.4 mm with no ulceration. Sentinel node biopsy did not show any evidence of positive lymph nodes and there were no systemic features to suggest distant metastases. The pathological staging of this tumour is
explanation: Stage Ila is Breslow thickness 1.01-2 mm with ulceration or a Breslow thickness between 2.01-4 mm without ulceration in the absence of clinical, radiographic or histological evidence of lymph node involvement. Stage lb is Breslow thickness less than 1 mm but with ulceration or mitoses equal to or more than 1 per mm2. Stage IV is presence of distant metastases. 150 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: The sensory innervation of the vertex of the scalp Is predominantly by which nerve?
explanation: Thi: supra-trochlear nerve innervates part of the frontal scalp. The auriculotemporal nerve innervates the parietal part and the lesser occipital parieto-occipital part of the scalp behind the ear.

question: A 17-year-old man presented with diffuse asymptomatic angiokeratomas on the trunk and genitalia with bilateral leg oedema. In addition he has been complaining of neuropathic pains in his limbs and hypohidrosis. Urinalysis showed evidence of proteinuria. Which of the following statements regarding this condition is incorrect?

choices.A: Cardiac arrhythmias are a potential complication in this condition
choices.B: The angiokeratomas tend not to respond to enzyme replacement therapy
choices.D: The disease is general:y milder in women
choices.E: The pattern of inheritance is autosomal dominant

correct_text: The pattern of inheritance is autosomal dominant
explanation: c; Fabry s disease is an X-linked recessive disorder. Female carriers can still manifest the disease but it tends to be milder. The angiokeratomas and lymphoedema generally do not respond to enzyme replacement therapy. Hypohidrosis and neuropathic pain crises are other manifestations of the disease.

question: A 40-year-old man with a history of thyroid carcinoma and multiple facial tricholemmomas presented with cobblestoning of the oral mucosa and palmo- plantar keratoses. The most likely diagnosis here is
explanation: The rare Cowden s syndrome should be suspected when a patient presents with oral cobblestoning, pa Imo-plantar keratoses, tricholemmomas and a history of internal malignany (mostly breast, thyroid or uterus). Muir-Torre syndrome can also be associated with internal malignancies but the cutaneous manifestations are of sebaceous tumours or eruptive keratoacanthomas. Gardner s syndrome is associated with polyposis coli (risk of colon carcinoma) and multiple epidermoid cysts and/or lipomas. Bazex syndrome is also called acrokeratosis paraneoplastica and is a paraneoplastic phenomenon that often presents with a psoriasiform appearance of the hands and feet accentuated around the nails with associated nail changes, palmo-plantar keratoderma and alopecia.

question: Cobblestoning of the gingiva can occur with all of the following except
explanation: Peutz-Jeghers syndrome is associated with intestinal polyps and typically presents with (peri)-oral lentigines. Other oral manifestations of Crohn s disease include aphthous ulcerations and granulomatous cheilitis. The cobblestoning in Darrer s disease is mostly apparent in the hard palate. 151 Section 1: Answers 8,. Comments

question: Dental anomalies can be found in all of the following except
explanation: In Netherton s syndrome there is ichthyosis with hair shaft defects but dental abnormalities are not a feature. Other conditions that can be associated with dental anomalies include ectodermal dysplasia, congenital erythropoietic porphyria, focal dermal hypoplasia, Sjogren- Larsson syndrome and Papiflon-Lefevre syndrome.

question: Which of the following nerves is not a branch of the ophthalmic division of trigeminal (Vl) nerve?
explanation: The infra-orbital nerve is a branch of the maxillary branch (V2) of the trigeminal nerve. Other branches of the maxillary branch (V2) include the zygomaticofacial and zygomaticotemporal nerves. The external nasal nerve is a branch of the ophthalmic division of trigeminal (Vl) nerve.

question: A 40-year-old man with a history of exce~sive alcohol intake and self- neglect has a 12-month history of intermittent scaling of his hands and feet associated with a malar rash on his cheeks and a powdery scale on his nose. In addition, he had marked erythema of his tongue and has been complaining of loose stools for several months. He scores low on mini mental state examination. The most likely diagnosis is
explanation: Pellagra is classically a disease of the 4 Ds : dermatitis, diarrhoea, dementia and death. It is due to deficiency in vitamin B3 (Niacin). Pellagra typically spares the nails and hair and can also be caused by deficiency in tryptophan. Photosensitivity is often present. 6-Mercaptopurine, isoniazid and 5-flurouracil are drugs that can in rare cases cause pellagra. Beriberi is due to deficiency in vitamin B1 (Thiamine) and typically gives oro-genital dermatitis with encephalopathy, cardiac failure and peripheral neuropathy.

question: A 50-year old man presented with non-tender papules and nodules with no surface changes on the back. He had recently been complaining of night sweats and weight loss. Histology of the lesion showed a dense dermal infiltrate which stained negative for CD3, CD20, CD79a, bcl-2, bcl-6, CD4, CD30 and CDS and was positive for CD43 and myeloperoxidase. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: The negative staining to the T-cell markers CD3, CD4 and CDS rules out mycosis fungoides. The negative staining to the B-cell markers CD20 and CD79a rules out cutaneous B cell lymphomas. CD43 positivity is a clue for myeloid leukaemia (leukaemia cutis in this case) in the absence of positivity to Band T cell markers. Myeloid leukaemia also stains positive to myeloperoxidase. 152 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: You remove a tumour from the right nasal ala and decide to reconstruct the defect with a full thickness skin graft. One of the following factors does not reduce the surviva I of the graft

choices.A: Cartilage at the base of the defect
choices.E: The presence of a fat layer at the base of the graft

explanation: Full thickness skin graft can be used as a method of reconstruction for certain defects particularly on the nasal alae, ears, lower eyelids and temple. Several factors ca! l influence the survival of the graft tissue and it is important to be aware of these. Donor sites skin should match the skin colour and texture of the recipient site and are is often harvested from the pre- or post-auricular or sites or from the supra-clavicular area.

question: A tumour was removed from the conch al bowl. This defect measures 10x8 mm and is fairly superficial with intact periosteum. Which of the following reconstructive options is the most suitable in this case
explanation: Secondary intention healing can be a suitable option particularly in the conchal bowl, medial ca nth us, scalp, forehead and the dorsum of the hands and feet. As the wound heals a degree of contraction will occur and it is essential to monitor that the contraction force does not result in an unwanted pull on a free margin such as the eyebrow or nasal ala.

question: Which of the following is an ablative laser?
explanation: Ablation is simply the removal of tissue and in the cases of laser ablation is due to vaporization of the tissue. Other ablative laser modality is carbon dioxide laser.

question: Which of the following is the most commonly observed side effect of pulsed dye laser treatment?
explanation: Bruising may last up to 2 weeks if a purpuric mode has been used. In some instances, if a non-purpuric mode (often with longer pulse duration and lower fluence) is used, results may take require several more treatments to achieve a similar outcomes as to the purpuric mode. All other side-effects mentioned in the answers are possible, but are less frequent. 153 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: You remove a suspicious mole on the shoulder of a young woman who had excessive sun exposure. The result showed a superficial spreading melanoma with a Breslow thickness of 0.7 mm with no mitoses or ulceration. You arrange for urgent action but the patient informs you that she is now 8 weeks pregnant. Which of the following actions should take place?

choices.A: Defer any further intervention until after delivery of the baby
choices.C: Wide local excision with 1 cm margin
choices.D: Wide local excision with 2 cm margin

correct_text: Wide local excision with 1 cm margin
explanation: Whilst it is good practice to defer most non-urgent and benign lesions removal till after delivery, pregnancy should not be a contra-indication for a wide local excision of a melanoma. Melanoma Is not very radiosensitive however adjunctive radiotherapy m y be used post positive sentinel lymph node lymphadenectomy particularly if there was ex tra-capsular spread of the tumour or more than 3 lymph nodes were involved.

question: You see a 61-year old Australian man with a 3 cm ulcerated nodule below his left eye that has been growing over the last 5 months. On further examination the nodule appears tethered and attached the underlying structures. A biopsy performed a week earlier showed a poorly-differentiated squamous cell carcinoma. What should be the next action?

choices.D: Surgical excision with a margin of 1 cm
choices.E: Surgical excision with a margin of 6 mm

explanation: In cases of skin tumours which are large and/or tethered and attached to underlying structures imaging should be arranged to assess for local Invasion.

question: Perineural Invasion Is typically not observed In which of the following
explanation: Perineural invasion portends a poorer prognosis with increased risk for recurrence and metastasis. Desmoplastic trichoepithelioma is a rare follicular tumour that histologically is in the differential of microcystic adnexal carcinoma and morphoeic basal cell carcinoma but typically, perineural invasion is not seen.

question: Which of the following is a sensory nerve?
explanation: All facial sensory nerves are branches of the trigeminal nerve. The motor nerves of the face are branches of the facial nerve and are the temporal, zygomatic, buccal, marginal mandibular, and cervical nerves. In facial skin surgery the 2 danger zones that every dermatologist should be aware of are the anatomic location of both the temporal and marginal mandibular nerves.

question: You diagnose a patient as having pemphigus foliaceous and send the histology specimen to the pathologist. If your clinical diagnosis is correct, he should identify the split at
explanation: Most patients with pemphigus vulgaris have mucosa! membrane erosions. The blisters of pemphigus vuigaris develop in the deeper portion of the epidermis, just above the basal cell layer. Patients with pemphigus foliaceus have only cutaneous involvement without mucosa! lesions, and the splits occur in the superficial part of the epidermis, mostly at the granular layer. 154 Section 1: Answers & Comments

question: The phenomenon by which gentle pressure on an intact bu Ila forces the fluid to spread under the skin away from the site of pressure in pemphigus Is known as
explanation: Due to the lac < of cohesion within the epidermis, its upper layers easily move laterally with slight pressure or rubbing in patients with active pemphigus. This is known as Nikolsky s sign.
