Neumann type follows more aggressive course and its treatment can be challenging. Oral corticosteroids, dapsone, azathioprine, retinoids, etanercept and extracorporeal photopheresis have been used. 217 Section 2: Answers & Comments

question: Following surgery for excision of a basal cell carcinoma, an 85-year old patient presents with asymmetrical smile. Injury to the following nerve is most likely
explanation: The marginal mandibular nerve lies along the body of the mandible (80%) or within 1-2 cm below (20%). Although it lies deep to the platysma throughout much of its course it becomes more superficial approximately 2 cm lateral to the corner of the mouth and ends on the under surface of the muscles. Injury to the marginal mandibular nerve results in paralysis of the depressors of the corner of the mouth.

question: A 35-year old woman has residual telangiectasiae and erythema following successiul treatment of the papulo-pustular element of rosacea wi~h iymecycline. She is keen for treatment of her facial telangiectasiae and erythema. Which of the following is the best treatment?
explanation: Pulsed dye laser at 595nm is the treatment of choice for most vascular lesions. Another laser that is commonly used for the treatment of telangiectasiae is the KTP laser (frequency doubled, Nd:YAG laser).

question: Which of the following can be used as a dep!gmenting agent in the treatment of vitiligo?
explanation: Monobenzyl ether of hydroquinone {Monobenzone) is used for depigmenting resid· ual normal skin in patients with extensive vitiligo. It Is a phenolic toxin that destroys epidermal melanocytes. It is available as a 20 percent cream. Allergic and irritant reactions may occur. 218 Section 2: Answers & Comments

question: Which of the following is associated with flagellate hyperpigmentation?
explanation: Certain drugs may produce a specific pattern of hyperpigmentation. Flagellate hyperpigmentation - bleomycin or zidovudine. Diffuse hyperpigmentation on the pr1lms and soles - cyclophosphamide or doxorubicin. Localized hyperpigmentation around small joints - bleomycin and doxorubicin. Melasma-like pigmentation-oestrogen-related hormonal substances and phenytoin-like medications. Nail unit involvement - zidovudine, psoralens, minocycline, antimalarials and Gold. Mucosal hyperpigmentation - cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, zidovudine, minocycline and some heavy metals. Blue-gray pigmer.taticn in sun-exposed areas - amiodarone. Yellow-brown to bluish-gray pigmentation on the face, the neck, the lower extremities, and the forearms - hydroxychloroquine. Exogenous ochronosis - chronic hydroquinone use. Bluish-gray pigmentation, especially in sun-exposed areas, and pigmentations of the conjunctivae - chlorpromazine and related phenothiazines. Skin, nails, scleral and oral mucosa!, thyroid, bones, and teeth hyperpigmentation - minocycline.

question: Which of the following Is the safest method of administering a drug to avoid sensitization?
explanation: Oral administration of a drug is least likely to produce sensitization. Intramuscular is the most likely parenteral way of eliciting drug sensitization.

question: A 40-year old rnan complains of recurrent burning eruption on the glans penis. Examination shows hyperpigmentation over the glans penis. He has had recurrent episodes over the past 2 years. Which of the following is most likely to be implicated?
explanation: This patient describes symptoms of a fixed drug eruption (FDE). FDE recurs at the same site with each administration of the drug. Most common sites for FDE include face and genitalia, but can occur anywhere. Localised erythema leading to blistering is commonly seen. Blistering may not always be present. Hyperpigmentation occurs following resolution of the erythema and blistering. Most commonly implicated medications include phenolphthalein in laxatives, sulphonamides, beta-lactams antibiotics, tetracyclines, barbiturates, gold, oral contraceptives and aspirin. 219 Section 2: Answers & Comments

question: A 60-year old man was admitted to ICU with sepsis. A few days later he developed pruritus and erythema over the upper trunk associated with angioedema. Which is the most likely cause of his symptoms?
explanation: Pruritus, erythema and angioedema over the upper body are associated with intravenous administration of vancomycin- the so-called red man syndrome. It is thought to be secondary to histamine release and can be prevented by administering antihistamines. Rifampicin has been reported to cause similar reactions.

question: A 45-year old patient with Darier's disease is referred for evaluation of nail changes. Which of the following is not a recognized feature of nail disease in Darier's disease?
explanation: The nails in Darier s disease are fragile and split easily. Other features include - combination of red and white longitudinal stripes (erytnro- and leukonychia). Distal V-shaped nick and subungual hyperkeratosis are commonly seen.

question: Which of the follow!ng is not true of Grover's disease?

choices.A: A history of sun-exposure is often forthcoming
choices.B: ATP2A2 mutations similar to Darier's disease have been identified
choices.C: Can resemble Darier's disease on histology
choices.D: Features of Hailey-Hailey disease may be seen on histology,
choices.E: The rash can be persistent in some patients

correct_text: ATP2A2 mutations similar to Darier's disease have been identified
explanation: Grover s disease (transient acantholytic dermatosis) presents as pruritic, papulovesicular eruption on the trunk. Seen in adults with a history of chronic sun damage. Histological examination shows variable focal acantholytic dyskeratosis resembling, Darier s disease, Hailey-Hailey disease or pemphigus. Classic (transient) form resolves within a few months, but a persistent form has been recognized. Unlike Darier s disease there is no evidence for genetic predisposition.

question: Which of the following types of porokeratoses is not associated with malignant epithelial neoplasm?
explanation: Malignant epithelial neoplasms are reported in all sub-types except the punctate variety. The risk is the highest with linear porokeratosis and giant porokeratosis of Mibelli. 220 Section 2: Answers & Comments

question: Fogo selvagem is a subtype of which of the following?
explanation: Fogo selvagem is an endemic form of pemphigus foliaceus. It is endemic in rural Brazil and it means wild fire in Portuguese. It is clinically, histologically, and lmmunopathologically similar to sporadic pemphigus foliaceus. The geographic distribution of disease clustering is similar to that of a black fly, Simulium nigrimanum.

question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?

choices.A: Guinea pig oesophagus is more sensitive for detecting pempiligus foliaceous antibodies
choices.B: lgG staining is present on the cell surface of epidermal cells in pemphigus vulgaris
choices.C: Monkey oesophagus is more sensitive for detecting pemphigus vulgaris antibodies
choices.D: Pemphigus vulgaris and foliaceous display similar direct immunofluorescence findings
choices.E: There is no correlation between the titre of circulating anti-celi surface antibody and disease activity in pemphigus vulgaris and foliaceous

correct_text: There is no correlation between the titre of circulating anti-celi surface antibody and disease activity in pemphigus vulgaris and foliaceous
explanation: It is usually not possible to differentiate between pemphigus vulgaris and foliaceous on immunofluoresence findings as it is similar in both disorders. lgG staining is present on the cell surface of epidermal cells throughout the epidermis in both disorders. In general, monkey oesophagus is more sensitive for detecting pemphigus vulgaris antibodies. Guniea pig oesophagus is a superior substrate for detecting pemphigus foliaceous antibodies. There is a positive, correlation between the titre of circulating anti-cell surface antibod { and the disease activity in pemphigus vulgaris and foliaceous. However, this correlation is not perfect (unlike in bullous pemphigoid where there is no correlation between the antibodies and disease activity). Disease activity in individual patient does not necessarily correlate with antibody titre; therefore, clinical findings should not be replaced by immunofluoresence titres in monitoring the disease.

question: Which of the following statements is true regarding drug-induced pemphigus?

choices.B: Patients do not exhibit auto-antibodies to desmoglein 1 and desmoglein 3
choices.C: Pemphigus foliaceous is the commonest morphological pattern
choices.D: Remission after drug withdrawal is uncommon

correct_text: Pemphigus foliaceous is the commonest morphological pattern
explanation: The prevalence of pemphigus in penlclllamlne users is estimated to be approximately 7 percent. Pemphigus foliaceous is more common than pemphigus vulgaris in these patients. Direct and indirect immunofluorescence are positive. Auto-antibodies to sporadic pemphigus antigens desmoglein 1 and desmoglein 3 have been noted. Most patients go into remission after stopping the offending drug. ACE inhibitors have been implicated in both pemphigus vulgaris and foliaceous. 221 Section 2: Answers & Comments

question: In which of the following syndromes are multiple fibrofolliculomas a pathognomonic feature?
explanation: N Fibrofolliculomas are tiny skin-colouied papules on the head, neck, and upper trunk. Birt-Hogg-Dube syndrome is an autosomal dominant condition caused by a mutation in the protein folliculin. Salient features include fibrofolliculomas, trichodiscomas, and acrochordons. Birt-Hogg-Dube syndrome is associated with an increased risk of renal carcinomas and pneumothoraces.

question: A-45 year old woman presents with a few months history of diffuse hair loss. She complains of losing a lot of hair whilst combing. Her past medical history includes breast cancer for which she has recently received chemotherapy. Examination shows diffuse non-scarring alopecia. What is the likely diagnosis?
explanation: Anagen effluvium is usually seen after cancer chemotherapy. Telogen effluvium can also result from cancer chemotherapy or stress. Anagen effluvium results from inhibition or arrest of cell division in the hair matrix which leads to narrow weakened segment of the hair shaft that is susceptible to fracture with minimal trauma. The characteristic finding in anagen effluvium is the tapered fracture of the hair shafts as a result of damage to the matrix. Anagen and telogen effluvium can be differentiated on pull test, where more anagen hair will be seen. Pull test is negative in diffuse alopecia areata. Exclamation hair mark hairs can be seen in alopecia areata.

question: In which of the following is Miescher radial granuloma a histopathological feature?
explanation: Miescher radial granuloma is composed of small, round, well-defined nodular aggregations of small histiocytes which are radially arranged around a minute slit. It is a characteristic histopathologic marker of erythema nodosum.

question: Which of the following is associated with black, necrotic palatal ulceration in insulin-dependent diabetics with poor diabetic control?
explanation: Rhinocerebral form of zygomycosls is associated with black, necrotic, palatal ulceration. It is associated with poorly controlled insulin-dependent diabetes and keto-acidosis. 222 Section 2: Answers & Comments

question: A 35-year-old East Timorian immigrant presents with multiple numerous, variable-sized erythematous and dusky annular macules, ill-defined patches and well-demarcated plaques scattered across the trunk, arms, proximal legs and the face. He complains of hand and feet numbness. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Diagnosis of leprosy is primarily clinical and is based on presence of one of following three features-hypcpigmented or erythematous patches with definite loss of sensation, thickened peripheral nerves and acid-fast bacilli on skin smears or biopsy material. Histology is the gold standard for diagnosis of leprosy. Identification of endoneuritis (nerve disruption and fragmentation) which can be difficult on haematoxylin and eosin is helped by S100 stain which enables differentiation of tuberculoid leprosy from other cutaneous granulomatous diseases.

question: Which of the following is the investigation of choice in fibromatosis colli?
explanation: Fibromatosis colli (sterr.omastoid tumour of infancy) is a self-limiting benign proliferation of fibroblasts in the lower one-third of the sternocleidomastoid muscle. Presentation is in the first few weeks of life and the lesion can grow rapidly causing marked expansion of the sternocleidomastoid. Clinical and radiographic differential diagnoses Include rhabdomyosarcoma or neuroblastoma. It is the most common cause of neonatal torticollis. It usually resolves within the first year of life. Excisional biopsy is not required except where malignancy is suspected. Fine-needle aspiration is the preferred diagnostic technique and shows clusters of benign, spindled, plump fibroblasts with ovoid to elongated nuclei.

question: Which of the following is not a feature of Conradi-Hunermann syndrome?
explanation: Conradi-Hunermann syndrome is an X-linked dominant disorder. Features include ichthyosiform scaling erythroderma patterned along the lines of Blaschke followed by bands of follicular atrophoderma, hyperpigmentation, cataracts, scarring alopecia, saddle-nose deformity, asymmetric limb reduction defects, and stippled calcifications of the epiphyses. It is lethal in homozygous males. Mutations occur in the emopamil binding protein gene at Xpll.23-pll.22.42. Ichthyosis, keratotic follicular plugging containing dystrophic calcification in newborns are also seen. 223 Section 2: Answers & Comments

question: A-26-year old lady was referred for patch testing with persistent hand and facial eczema for the last year, which responds only partially to topical steroids and emollients. She had strong positive reactions to formaldehyde 1% on patch testing. Avoidance advice should be given for which of the following chemicals?
explanation: Patients who are allerg;c to formaldehyde should avoid the formaldehyde releasers which include Quaternium 15, imidazo!idinyl urea, DMDM Hydantoin and diazolidinyl urea. Mercaptobenzothiazole is a rubber accelerator and reacts with carba mix and thiurams.

question: A 45-year old woman presented with red, pruritic and swollen rash on the periorbital area, scalp and forehead. She had applied a hair dye 2 days before the onset of the rash. Patch testing demonstrates that she is allergic to para-phenyla!Tline diamine (PPD). PPD can cross-react with the following
explanation: PPD cross-reacts with several other para-amino groups such as PADA, benzocaine and azo-dyes.

question: A neonate is born with distinctive features of harlequin ichthyosis. The gene defect is?
explanation: ATP2Cl is the gene defect in Hailey-Hailey disease. The gene defect in lamellar ichthyosis is TGM1 (transglutamlnase 1). NEMO is the gene defect in Incontinentia pigmenti and stands for NFKB Essential Modulator.

question: An 8-year old boy presented with his mother with a history of extreme photosensitivity with a burning and painful sensation within minutes following sun exposure. He had on several occasions, been noted to have swelling of the hands following sun exposure. His elder brother has similar symptoms and is currently taking beta-carotene tablets. The enzyme defect in this condition is
explanation: Ferrochelatase is the enzyme defect in erythropoietic protoporphyrla which typically presents with pain and burning sensation, extreme sun sensitivity within minutes to exposure of sunlight and may be associated with swelling of the hands. Protoporphyrinogen oxidase is the enzyme defect in variegate porphyria. Uroporphyrinogen decarboxylase is the enzyme defect in porphyria cutanea tarda. In hereditary coproporphyria the defect is in coproporphyrinogen oxidase.

question: A 55-year old lady is undergoing excision of an atypical naevus on her shoulder. You are about to inject 2% lignocaine with adrenaline. Contra-indication for this anaesthetic would include?
explanation: Anaesthetic solutions containing adrenaline should not be used if patients are taking non-selective beta-blockers, such as propranolol. In these situations plain lignocaine should be used instead. N A risk of developing a hypotensive crisis is small, nevertheless it is considered good and safe practice to enquire about medications; in particular, for propranolol. 224 Section 2: Answers & Comments

question: A 40-year old man has had two sebaceous carcinomas excised within the last 3 years and reports that both his father and sister have had several sebaceous carcinomas and sebaceous adenomas excised. The most common malignancy associated with this disorder Is
explanation: Muir-Torre syndrome is an autosomal dominant syndrome where patients develop sebaceous adenomas or carcinomas and this is associated with intern2l malignancies with colorectal cancers accounting for nearly half of all the tumours. Genito-urinary, breast and lung cancers can also occur with this disease. Sebaceous hyperplasia is not associated with Muir-Torre syndrome.

question: Q-Switched alexandrite laser is reported to be useful for removal of green tattoos. The wave length of Q-Switched alexandrite laser is
explanation: Q-Switched Ruby laser has a wave length of 694 nm whilst Erbium YAG has a wavelength of 2940 nm. CO2 laser has a wavelength the far infrared region of 10600 nm.

question: In the United Kingdom, lmiquimod cream (aldara) is not licensed for treatment of which of the following conditions?
explanation: lmiquimod cream can be used for Bowen s disease; however this is an unlicensed treatment in this condition. Its current licence is for genital warts, superficial basal cell carcinoma and actinic keratoses.

question: A 36-year old man has been treated successfully with a systemic agent for his blistering disorder and reports a gradual weakness of his right foot, resulting in him tripping over several times. On examination, there was demonstrable motor weakness, with intact sensation. Which of the following drugs is most likely to be implicated in this case?
explanation: Dapsone is an antagonist of dihydropteroate synthetase and prevents the formation of folic acid. It can be used in several blistering disorders, and motor-neuropathy is one of its possible long-term complications. Hydroxychloroquine can cause retinopathy and this needs to be monitored for regularly. Mepacrine is an anti-malarial drug, often used in conjunction with or as an alternative to hydroxychloroquine but does not cause ocular toxicity. 225 Section Z: Answers & Comments

question: A 45-year old man is admitted with severe desquamation of his skin following ingestion of phenytoin for epilepsy. Your consultant decides to start him on ! ntravenous immunoglobulin. In the United Kingdom, intravenous immunoglobulins are licensed for use in which of the following conditions?
explanation: Intravenous immunoglobulins are used in several de;matological diseases, which include toxic epidermal necrolysis, pemphigus vulgaris, dermatomyositis and Kawasaki disease. Currently, it only has a licence for use in Kawasaki disease among the dermatological conditions.

question: A 34-year old lady presented with a long-standing painful ulcer on the lateral aspect of the right lower leg which has been pres em for 6 months and did not respond to various dressings and compression bandages. On examination, there was evidence of liveao reticularis on the lower legs and the patient gives a history of a previous pulmonary embolism and two spontaneous miscarriages. Laboratory examination showed mild thrombocytosis. The most likely diagnosis here is
explanation: Painful chronic ulcers in young people can be secondary to vasculitis, and in this case, the presence of livedo reticularis, history of pulmonary embolism and miscarriages is highly suggestive of anti-phospholipid syndrome. Investigations should include a full vasculitis screen and auto-antibodies which include anti-cardiolipin and anti-phospholipid antibodies. Treatment with aspirin should be commenced. This condition can co-exist with systemic lupus erythematosus. Cryoglobulinaemia can present with livedo reticularls and vasculitic lesions. These tend to be acral and exacerbated on exposure to cold temperatures. Although this would still be a possibility in this patient, anti-phospholipid syndrome is more likely due to the history of miscarriages and pulmonary emboll. Henoch-Schonlein purpura is a form of vasculitis where immune complexes with predominantly lgA antibodies occur in the buttocks and legs, and may be associated with throat, abdominal pain, arthralgia and renal involvement. Around 1% of patients may progress to develop end stage renal failure.

question: A 56-year old man presented with bilateral eczema affecting the dorsal aspects of his feet and has been present since he started wearing a pair of new shoes. It has been treated witr, topical steroids and he was referred for patch testing. The most likely allergen in this case would be
explanation: Potassium dich;omate is often the cause of shoe allergy, as it is used for tanning of the leathers. It can also be found in cement, and may often cross react with nickel sulphate and cobalt chloride. Potassium di chromate can be an irritant, and if this is suspected, then testing to a lower concentration should be done. 226 Section 2: Answers & Comments

question: A 28-year old man who has been on penicillamine for several years presented with an asymptomatic annular eruption on the right side of the neck which consists of keratotic papules. There is no associated scaling or erythema. The most likely diagnosis is
explanation: Elastosis perforans serpiginosa is a disorder in which there is trans-epidermal illumination of elastic fibres. Although the condition may occur spontaneously, this can also occur secondary to penicillamine or in patients with Marfan s or Ehler s-Danlos syndrome. The clinical description does not tit with the other diagnoses mentioned (e.g. granuloma annulare does not have a keratotic surface).

question: A 37-year old lady was referred to the dermatology department with a 3-year history of urticaria! lesions that failed to respond to various anti-histamines given by her GP. Further history reveals that the individual wheals persist for days before they disappear. This often leaves post-inflammatory pigmentation. There is also associated bone pain and an associated paraproteinaemia. The most likely diagnosis here is
explanation: Schnitzler s syndrome is a rare disorder which is characterised by the presence of urticaria I-like lesions that often persist for days or even weeks, and is associated with bone pain and paraproteinaemia. Bone pain can often be severe. Muckle-Wells syndrome can present with limb pain and an urticarial-like eruption, however, this is often associated with recurrent fever, amyloidosis and deafness. This is an autosomal dominant disorder due to CIASl defect. Although urticaria! vasculitis can present with urticaria! lesions that persist for days leaving post inflammatory hyperpigmentation, this is often associated with arthralgia, rather than bone pain.

question: A 34-year old lady has been troubled with persistent acne over the last 10 years with hirsutism, hair loss and menstrual irregularities. Polycystic ovarian syndrome has been excluded by various hormonal testing and imaging by the gynaecologist. She is on a number of medications, one of which could be the cause of her symptoms. Which of the following medications is most likely to be associated with these symptoms?
explanation: Sodium valproate is an anti-epileptic and can rarely produce an acneiform eruption together with a clinical and biochemical picture that is similar to polycystic ovarian syndrome. Lithium and prednisolone can both cause acneiform eruptions, however, this if often monomorphic in nature and would not explain the signs of hyperandrogenism. Minocycline can be used in acne; the possible side effects are a lupus-like syndrome, hepatitis and pigmentation.

question: A 64-year old man has two patches of Bowen's disease on the left lower leg, previously treated with cryotherapy with little success. A consultant dermatologist suggested treatment with photodynamic therapy and the use of methyl levulenic acid (MAL). What should be the approximate application time of the MAL for treatment with a light source?
explanation: The ideal application time for MAL is 3 hours, to ensure maximum affectivity. Shorter duration of application may result in Ineffective therapy. 227 Section 2: Answers & Comments

question: A 26-year old man of Jewish origin developed multiple shallow painful erosions in his mouth, multiple erosions on his trunk and limbs that start as flaccid bullae. Multiple swabs taken from the bullae and erosions showed commensals only. He has been referred for a diagnostic biopsy, including immunofluorescence. Histological appearance of the biopsy would be

choices.C: Acanthosis and spongiosis throughout the epidermis

explanation: The diagnosis is pemphigus vulgaris and therefore when blistering diseases are suspected, immunofluorescence samples should be taken. In the case of pemphigus vulgaris, classic histological appearance would be of acantholysis and intra-epidermal blistering with positive immunofluorescence within the epidermis. In pemphigus foliaceus, the split would be in the subcorneal layer with mucosa! involvement being typically absent. The desmoglein is of type 1 in pemphigus foliaceus and is predominantly of type 3 in pemphigus vulgaris; however, desmoglein 1 can also be involved.

question: A 26-year old lady with a history of photosensitivity developed an annular erythematous rash with scaling, predominantly on her shoulders and upper chest following exposure to sunlight. Her laboratory investigations showed a strong positivity to the anti-Ro antibody. She wishes to become pregnant in the near future and has asked whether the foetus can come to any harm. Which of the following statement is true?

choices.C: There is a small risk of congenital heart block of the foetus
choices.D: There is risk of cleft lip to the foetus
choices.E: This condition and laboratory findings have no effect on the pregnancy

correct_text: There is a small risk of congenital heart block of the foetus
explanation: Subacute lupus erythematosus and a positive Ro antibody indicate a strong degree of photosensitivity and the risk of developing a congenital heart block in the foetus. Close collaboration with the obstetricians is required. There is also a risk of neonatal lupus erythematosus; however, this is often transient and will disappear within the first few months of life due to the passive transfer of lgG antibodies.

question: A 17-year old girl has developed very painful erosions in the vulva one week following unprotected sexual intercourse with a new partner. Close examination showed a few intact vesicles on an erythematous base and few eroded areas where previous vesicles were present. The most likely pathogen in this case is
explanation: Although traditional teaching is that herpes simplex virus type 1 is predominantly implicated in orolabial herpes and herpes simplex type 2 in genital herpes, both conditions can be caused by either viral serotypes. Variceila-zoster virus is implicated in shingles, and whilst there are some reports of painful ulceration with fever in females with Epstein Barr Virus. The morphology of grouped vesicles on an erythematous base is characteristic of herpes simplex infection. 228 Section 2: Answers & Comments

question: A 60-year old man who is on warfarin for metallic aortic valve replacement presents with a 1.5cm nodular basal cell carcinoma on the dorsal aspect of his hand. He is very reluctant to have this treated surgically and wishes for alternative treatment. You discuss the option of radiotherapy and have decided to refer him to the radiotherapist. Which mode of radiotherapy is used for the treatment of basal cell carcinoma?
explanation: Radiotherapy can be used for basal cell and squamous cell carcinomas if there are contra-indications for surgery. Superficial x-ray is the treatment of choice in basal cell carcinoma with the use of high dose radical radiation. Brachytherapy is a method used where an implant is placed followed by high dose radiation. This is often used for Kaposi s sarcoma. Photodynamic therapy can be used for superficial basal cell carcinomas but not those of the nodular type.

question: You demonstrate to a group of medical students that detachment of the P.pidermis can occur with gentle lateral pressure in certain dermatological conditions. This sign is positive in which of the following conditions?
explanation: The Nikolsky s sign is positive when gentle lateral pressure on the skin leads to shearing/detachment of the epidermal component. Second degree burns can also exhibit the Nlkolsky s sign.

question: A 50-year old man presents with peri-anal ulceration. The differential diagnosis of such ulceration includes
explanation: A detailed history and skin examination is required to assess or obtain any valuable clues to the possible aetiology of chronic peri-anal ulceration. Viral infections such as cytomegalovirus and herpes simplex virus should be suspected in immunocompromised patients. Squamous cell carcinoma should be included in the differential- particularly if human papillomavirus infection is a risk. Active underlying Crohn s disease can lead to metastatic disease which can present with ulceration. The histology in this case will show granulomas. Genital involvement in Crohn s is often accompanied by oedema. Nicorandil use has been increr1si! lgly recognized to cause mucosal and cutaneous ulcerations, including in ·peri-stomal sites. 229 Section 2: Answers & Comments

question: A 45-year old patient is commenced on a nEw systemic medication. He returns 2 weeks later complaining of breathlessness and appears cyanosed. A blood film demonstrates methaemoglobulinaemla. Which of the following drugs used in certain dermatological conditions can cause methaemoglobulinaemia?
explanation: Dapsone can cause haemclysis and methaemoglobulinaemia. Any patient who becomes breathless or cyanosed on dapsone must have his MetHb levels checked. Methotrexate can cause pulmonary fibrosis (most commonly seen in patients with rheumatoid arthritis) and drug-Induced pneumonitis, but can not cause methaemoglobulinaemla. Fumaric acid esters can cause gastro-intestinal symptoms, flushing and a drop in the lymphocyte count. Ciclosporin can cause hypertension and renal impairment and these should be regularly monitored.

question: A patient is referred to you for assessment of bluish discolouration of his proximal fingernails. "Blue lanulae" of the nails can occur with which of the fcBowing?
explanation: Mepacrine use can also give a blue-grey discolouration of the hard palate. Potassium permanganate soaks can give rise to brown nails. Tetracycline can cause photo-onycholysis which may be the sole manifestation of phototoxicity. Pseuciomonas aeruglnosa infection can give rise to green discolouration of the nai:s. Darier s disease may have longitudinal erythro- and/or leukonychia.

question: Cataracts are a feature of which of the following dermatological conciitions?
explanation: Other conditions which can be associated with cataracts are Gorlin s syndrome, incontinentia pigmenti, Neurofibromatosis type-2, trichothiodystrophy, vitamin B12 deficiency, Werner s syndrome, Refsum disease, Conradi-Hunermann syndrome, oral steroid use and PUVA therapy. Beh et s disease can be associated with uveitis, retinal vasculitis and hypopyon. Mucous membrane pemphigoid can cause symblepharon. Juvenile xanthogranulomas can be associated with glaucoma. Reiter s disease is associated with conjunctivitis. 230 Section 2: Answers & Comments

question: Which of the following antibiotics in the treatment of acne is associated with the least resistance?
explanation: Antibiotic resistance is a growing problem in the treatment of acne. It should be suspected in patients unresponsive to appropriate antibiotic therapy after 6 weeks of treatment. Propionibacterium acne resistance has been documented with all macrolides and tetracyclines used in the treatment of acne. Overall resistance is the highest with erythromycln and lowest with minocycline. Measures to avoid antibiotic resistance should include avoidance of antibiotic monotherapy, limiting long-term use of antibiotics, and combining antibiotics with benzyl peroxide. Recent studies do not show any benefit of using minocycline over other tetracyclines.

question: Which of the following genes is defective in Darier's disease?

choices.B: Calcium pump of the Golgi apparatus

explanation: Darier s disease and Hailey-Hailey disease are acantholytic disorders. Calcium pump of the sarco/ endoplasmic reticulum is defective in Darier s disease. Defect in calcium pump of the Golgi apparatus results in Hailey-Hailey disease. loss of function mutations in ATP2A2, which encodes sarco/endoplasmic reticulum Ca2+ adenosine triphosphatase (ATPase) isoform 2 (SERCA2), a calcium pump transporting Ca2+ from the cytosol to the lumen of the endoplasmic reticulum results in Darier s disease.

question: Defective calcium pump is not implicated in the pathogenesis of which of the following?
explanation: Darier White disease, epidermal dyskeratotic acantholytic naevi (localized form of Darier disease caused by somatic mosaicism), and aAcrokeratosis verruciformis of Hopf are caused by defects in the same gene encoding calcium pump of the endoplasmic reticulum. Hailey-Hailey disease results from defective calcium pump of the Golgi apparatus. 231 Section 2: Answers & Comments

question: The maximum adult dose for plain lignocaine as a local anaesthetic is
explanation: Lignocaine is widely used as a local anaesthetic in dermatology and the maximum safe volumes need to be known. ,., For plain lignocaine, the maximum safe adult does is 3mg/kg, however this is 7mg/kg when mixed with adrenaline. This is based on 1% llgnocaine concentration. Symptoms of lignocaine toxicity include drowsiness, tingling, numbness of the lips, tinnitus and a metallic taste. In severe toxicity, convulsions and respiratory arrest can occur. 1 ml of 1% lignocaine contains 10 mg of lignocaine.

question: The least painful local anaesthetic is
explanation: o.s% plain lignocaine is the least painful of the local anaesthetics; however, its action may be too short for complicated procedures. 1% lignocaine combined with adrenaline has a longer action; larger amounts are required for reaching the maximum safe volume compared to 2% lignocaine with adrenaline. Bupivacaine has a prolonged duration of action and is therefore used for long procedures and post-operative analgesia.

question: Which of the following is thought to be secondary to mycobacterium tuberculosis infection?
explanation: Erythema induratum of Bazin and nodular vasculitis describe the most common form of lobular panniculitis with vasculitis. The term erythema induratum of Bazin is used for cases in which an aetiologic relationship with tuberculosis is demonstrated. Presents as erythematous subcutaneous nodules and plaques on the posterior aspects of the lower legs, which may ulcerate and heal with scarring. Polymerase chain reaction may demonstrate mycobacterium tuberculosis DNA In skin biopsy specimens of patients with erythema induratum of Bazin. A full course of anti-tubercu:osis triple-agent therapy should be instituted when mycobacterium tuberculosis DNA is isolated. Other therapeutic measures include potassium iodide, supporting bandages, bed rest, and non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs. 232 Section 2: Answers & Comments

question: Which of the following is associated with "leopard skin" pattern of de pigmentation?
explanation: Several infections can result in pigmentary changes in the skin. Onchocercal depigmentation or leopard skin is the commonest feature of onchocerciasis and is rarely associated with pruritus. It presents as hypopigmented patches with perl-follicular spots of normally pigmented skin, typically on the pre-tibial area of older people in endemic areas.

question: Which type of collagen is the most abundant in the dermis?
explanation: The dermis is composed of type 1 collagen that forms nearly 80%, with nearly 15- 20% type 3 collagen and a small amount of type 5 collagen. Collagens provide the tensile strength in the dermis, whereas the elastic fibres provide the elasticity of the dermis. The origin of the collagen is from the fibroblasts which are found in the dermis. There are 2.8 types of collagen.

question: A 63-year old man presented with a nodular oasal cell carcinoma on the left side of his forehead above his eyebrow which was excised. Two weeks following the excision, he is still complaining of the inability to raise r1is left eyebrow which results in a droopy left eyebrow. Which nerve has been damaged during the procedure?

choices.B: Marginal mandibular branch of facial nerve

explanation: The temporal branch of the facial nerve innervates the frontalis and the upper portion of the orbicularis oculi. Damage to the marginal mandibular branch of the facial nerve will result in drooping of the mouth and the inability to evert the lip laterally and inferiorly. Damage to the great auricular nerve will result in numbness of the inferior two thirds of the ear and the adjacent cheek and neck area. Damage to the spinal accessory nerve will result In a winged scapula (the inability to shrug the shoulder and abduct the arm).

question: Which of the following is not a feature of Piebaldism?

choices.E: Sparing of hands and feet Section Z: Paper

explanation: Piebaldism is caused by mutations in the KIT proto-oncogene. Depigmented patches are present on the ventral or lateral trunk. Hands and feet are spared. Poliosis is common. Deafness is not a feature. Piebaldism with deafness is known as Woolf syndrome. 233 Section 2: Answers & Comments

question: Which of the following subtypes of Waardenburg syndrome has Hirschsprung disease as an additional feature?
explanation: Waardenburg syndrome type 4, is caused by heterozygous mutations in the transcription factor gene SOX10 or by homozygous mutations in the gene encoding the peptide ligand endothelin-3, EDN3, or its receptor, EDNRB. These genes are important in melanocyte development and in the development of the distal aspect of enteric nervous system cells. Waardenburg syndrome type 4 has features of Waardenburg syndrome type 1 (pigmentary abnormalities, dystopia canthorum, broadening of the nasal root, the presence of hypoplastic alae nasi, synophrys, poliosis, heterochromia irides, partial heterochromia irides, or hypoplastic blue irides, premature greying and congenital deafness). In addition it is associated with Hirschsprung disease (congenital aganglionosis of the colon).

question: Pulmonary fibrosis is a clinical feature of which of the following?
explanation: Hermansky-Pudlak syndrome (HPS) patients have oculocutaneous albinism with vari• able hypopigmentation of the skin, hair, and irides, and ocular abnormalities. Additional features include lack of platelet dense bodies, prolonged bleeding time, mucous membrane bleeding, and a predisposition to epistaxis, easy bruising, and metromenorrhagia. Pulmonary fibrosis is a common and severe manifestation of HPSl and HPS4. Pulmonary fibrosis causes death between the fourth and sixth decades of life. 234 Section 2: Answers & Comments

question: A 13-year old girl presents with multiple skin coloured nodules on the skin. In addition she has numerous coffee-coloured patches and macules on her skin. Her mother has similar patches on her skin. You diagnose the condition as neurofibromatosis type 1. Which of the following is the earliest skin sign of this condition?
explanation: The diagnostic criteria for neurofibromatosis-1 are: - 6 or more cafe-au-lait macules of >5 mm In greatest diameter in pre-pubertal children and >15 mr., i:1 post-pubertal individuals. - 2 or more neurofibromas of any type or 1 plexiform neurofibroma. - Freckling in axillary or inguinal regions. - 2 or more Lisch nodules. - Optic gliomas. - Osseous lesions including sphenoid dysplasia or thinning of long bone cortex with or without pseudoarthrosis. - First degree relative with NF-1. ,., At least two of the above criteria should be present to make a diagnosis of NF-1. ,., Cafe-au-la it macules are sharply defined, light brown patches which may be present at birth or appear shortly after - noted in all children with NF-1 by the age of 4 years. ,., Neurofibromas start to develop around puberty.

question: Which of the following does not exhibit antibodies to BPAG2 or its metabolic products?
explanation: Antibodies against BPAG2 or !ts metabolic products are seen in patients with bullous pemphigoid, pemphigoid gestationis, linear lgA disease, cicatricial pemphigoid, and lichen planus pemphigoides. The clinical appear.mce, immunofluoresence and type of infiltrate can help differentiate between these conditions (e.g. neutrophilic infiltrate in linear lgA as opposed to eosinophilic in bullous pemphigoid).

question: Which of the following statements regarding myasthenia gravis, thymoma and pemphigus is false?

choices.A: Irradiation of thymus or thymectomy may not improve the pemphigus disease activity
choices.B: Myasthenia gravis and thymoma are associated with pemphigus vulgaris and pemphigus foliaceous
choices.C: The course of myasthenia gravis follows the course of pemphigus
choices.D: Thymic abnormality may either precede or follow the onset of pemphigus
choices.E: Thymoma may be associated with paraneoplastic pemphigus

correct_text: The course of myasthenia gravis follows the course of pemphigus
explanation: Myasthenia gravis, thymoma, or both have been associated with pemphigus vulgaris and pemphigus foliaceous. Thymoma may be associated with PV and PF and with paraneoplastic pemphigus. ,., The course of myasthenia gravis is independent of pemphigus. ,., Thymic abnormality may either precede or follow the onset of pemphigus. Irradiation of thymus or thymectomy may not improve pemphigus disease activity. 235 Section 2: Answers & Comments

question: Which of the following statements regarding para neoplastic pemphigus is false?

choices.A: Antibodies to plakin family proteins are characteristic
choices.B: Blistering, lichenoid, or erythema multiforme-like iesions may be seen
choices.C: High fatality from disease complications, including pulmonary involvement with respiratory failure
choices.D: Most common underlying malignancy is thymoma

correct_text: Most common underlying malignancy is thymoma
explanation: para neoplastic pemphigus is a rare complication of malignancies of which non- Hodgkin lymphoma or chronic lymphocytic leukaemia are the commonest. Painful, erosive stomatitis is commonly seen. Polymorphous cutaneous lesions including blisters and erosions may be seen in addition to morbilliform, or lichenoid lesions. Anti-plakin antibodies are detected by indirect immunofluorescence against rodent bladder epithelium. There is high fatality from disease complications, Including sepsis, pulmonary involvement with respiratory failure or bronchiolitis obliterans.

question: Which of the following is associated with increased risk of internal malignancy?
explanation: The relative risk for cancer increases with anti-epillgrin cicatricial pemphigoid. The time between blister onset and cancer diagnosis is approximately 14 months. The risk for cancer appears higher in the first year of disease. Relative risk for malignancy with anti-epiligrin clcatrlcial pemphigoid approximates that for adults with dermatomyositis.

question: Which of the following is not a feature of Brunsting-Perry pemphigoid?

choices.A: Head and neck involvement is common

explanation: Brunsting-Perry pemphigoid is a locally recurrent and scarring sub-epidermal blistering disorder. Head or neck involvement is common. Patients are typically elderly. Brunsting-Perry pemphigoid predominates in elderly men. Mucous membrane involvement is uncommon. 236 Section 2: Answers & Comments

question: Which of the following is not true regarding pemphigoid gestationis?

choices.B: Direct immunofluorescence shows linear deposition of immunoglobulin G without C3
choices.C: Newborns may be affected with bullous lesions
choices.E: Usually occurs in the second-third trimester

correct_text: Direct immunofluorescence shows linear deposition of immunoglobulin G without C3
explanation: Pemphigoid gestationis (PG) is a pruritic, vesiculobullous eruption of acute-onset. Seen in the second-third trimester or the immediate postpartum period. Flares may occur around delivery. Shows a strong association with HLA-DR3, -DR4, and a C4 null allele. First onset usually on the abdomen and umbilicus. Spares the face, mucous membranes, palms, and soles. Newborns may be affected. Histopathology shows dermo-epidermal separation with numerous eosinophils. Direct immunofluorescence shows linear deposition of C3 (almost 100%), with or without immunoglobulin G. Indirect IF only occasionally detects circulating lgG deposition. Sera from most PG patients react to a 180-kd transmembrane protein with a collagenous domain. No significant maternal morbidity or mortality. Associated with a slight increase in premature and small-for-gestational-age births.

question: Which of the following is true regarding the prognosis of Pemphigoid gestation is?

choices.B: May flare in the post-partum period
choices.E: Recurrence>s are rare with oral contraceptive and menstruation

correct_text: May flare in the post-partum period
explanation: Pemphigoid gestationis has a variable clinical presentation and course. Spontaneous resolution during the latter part of gestation is common but dramatic post-partum flares may be seen. Recurrences with menstruation and flares with use of oral contraceptives occur in at least 25%. Spontaneous disease regression may occur during the third trimester but the disease may flare during parturition. 237 Section 2: Answers & Comments

question: Which of the following systemic diseases Is most commonly associated with epidermolysis bullosa acquisita?
explanation: Epidermolysis bullosa acquisita may be associated with various autoimmune systemic diseases: Inflammatory bowel disease (commonest). Systemic lupus erythematosus. Amyloidosis. Thyroiditis. Multiple endocrinopathy syndrome. Rheumatoid arthritis. Pulmonary fibrosis. Chronic lymphocytic leukemia. rhymoma. Diabetes mellitus.

question: Which of the following wavelengths is responsible for immediate tanning?
explanation: Immediate tanning occurs within 5 to 10 minutes of exposure to UVA irradiation (often referred to as immediate pigment darkening IPD ). It represents melanosomal relocation from the perikaryon to melanocytlc dendrites. It fades within minutes to days. It does not provide photoprotection and does not increase epidermal melanin level. It is predominantly visible in darker individuals.

question: Which of the following ls not a ubiquitous component of the basement membrane?
explanation: Basement membranes contain collagenous and non-collagenous glycoproteins and proteoglycans. Collagen IV, laminin, nidogen, and heparan sulfate proteoglycan perlecan are ubiquitially present in all basement membrane.

question: Which ofthe following results from altered a6~4 integrin?
explanation: Keratin 5 and 14 mutations result in epidermolysis bullosa simplex. Collagen XVII/BP180 - Linear lgA disease. Collagen VII - Epidermolysis bullosa acquisita. Laminin 332/laminin-5 - Junctional epidermolysis bullosa - Herlitz and non-Herlitz. a6 4 integrin - Cicatritial pemphigoid. 238 Section 2: Answers & Comments

question: Which of the following statements is false?

choices.A: ELISA can differentiate pemphigus vulgaris from pemphigus foliaceous
choices.B: ELISA is more sensitive than indirect immunofluoresence for pemphigus vulgaris and pemphigus folicaeous
choices.C: ELISA is positive for both desmogleins 3 and 1 in pemphigus vulgaris
choices.D: ELISA is positive for desmoglein 1 In mucosa! pemphigus vulgaris
choices.E: ELISA is positive for only desmoglein 1 in pemphigus foliaceous Sl!ctlon 2: Answen & Comment,

correct_text: ELISA is positive for desmoglein 1 In mucosa! pemphigus vulgaris
explanation: Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) is more sensitive and specific than immunofluorescence in differentiating pemphigus vulgaris from pemphigus foliaceous. ELISA titer correlates better than that of indirect immunofluorescence with disease activity. ELISA is positive for desmoglein 3 (but not desmoglein 1) in mucosal pemphigus vulgaris. ELISA is positive for both desmogleins 3 and 1 in pemphigus vulgaris with both mucosa! and skin involvement. ELISA is positive for only desmoglein 1 in PF. 239 Section 3: Paper 2 Section 3: Paper 2

question: Photosensitivity is not a presenting feature of one of the following?
explanation: Acute intermittent porphyria results from defects in porphobilinogen-deaminase. - Attacks are characterised by abdominal pain, psychiatric symptoms and peripheral neuropathy. There are no skin manifestations in acute intermittent porphyria. Variegate porphyria presents similarly to PCT but with the presence of acute symptoms; therefore it is essential to exclude this diagnosis in patients suspected of PCT through urine porphyrin measurements together with a plasma porphyrin scan.

question: A 48-year old alcoholic man was admitted with ascites and decompensated liver failure. He was noted to have a purpuric, perifollicular eruption on his legs. Significant bruising was also noted on his abdomen. What investigation would you request to make the diagnosis?

choices.E: Urine dip stick for protein and blood

explanation: Scurvy is characterized by general weakness, anaemia, gingivitis and petichieae. It is caused by a prolonged deficiency of vitamin C (ascorbic acid) in the diet. Vitamin C plays a crucial role in the formation of collagen. It is uncommon in modern society but can still be encountered in high risk population which includes institutionalised patients and alcoholics. Skin signs of scurvy include perifollicular hyperkeratotic papules, often on the shins. - These appear as reddish/bluish bruise-like spots surrounding hair follicles. The central hairs are twisted like corkscrews that may break easily. The papules may join together to form large areas of palpable purpura or ecchymoses. Diagnosis is based on clinical findings. Plasma ascorbic acid level may help in establishing the diagnosis, but this level tends to reflect the recent dietary intake rather than the actual tissue levels of vitamin C. Signs of scurvy can occur with low-normal serum levels of vitamin C. The level of vitamin C in leukocytes more accurately correlates to tissue stores compared with serum levels because these cells are not affected acutely by circadian rhythm or dietary changes. Confirmation of the diagnosis can be achieved by resolution following vitamin Cad ministration. 271 Section 3: Answers & Comments

question: A 70-year old woman is admitted with tense blisters developing on a background of eczematous skin. A skin biopsy is performed for histology and immunofluoresence. Histology confirms your diagnosis of bullous pemphigoid. Which of the following statements is true of immunofluoresence in bullous pemphigoid?

choices.A: Approximately 50% of patients have circulating anti-basement membrane zone lgG
choices.B: Bullous pemphigoid lgG causes complement activation by the alternate pathway
choices.C: C3 may be the sole immunoreactant on direct immunofluorescence of peri-lesional skin
choices.D: Indirect immunofluorescence antibody titer correlates with disease activity
choices.E: On lM NaCl induced blister, bullous pemphigoid antibodies bind to the floor of the blister

correct_text: C3 may be the sole immunoreactant on direct immunofluorescence of peri-lesional skin
explanation: In pemphigoid, direct immunofluorescence of peri-lesional skin reveals linear deposition of lgG and C3 at the epidermal basement membrane. Although both C3 and lgG are detected in most patients, C3 may be the sole immunoreactant. Approximately 70 - 80 % of patients with bullous pemphigoid have circulating anti-basement membrane zone lgG. On artificially splitting the skin with 1M NaCl, bullous pemphigoid antibodies bind to the roof of the blister while epidermolysis bullosa acquisita antibodies bind to the floor of the blister. In bullous pemphigoid, the indirect immunofluorescencE antibody titer does not usually correlate with disease extent or activity. Bullous pemphigoid lgG causes complement activation by the classic pathway, with activation of the alternative pathway by the C3 amplification mechanism.

question: A 27-year old woman with a long history of chronic plaque psoriasis has been suffering from an exacerbation of the disease with plaques covering approximately 40% of her body surface area. Her previous therapies included topical corticosteroids and phototherapy. She is due to get married in 2 months and is requesting a treatment that can rapidly help clear her psoriasis before her wedding. She is otherwise well with no co-morbidities. The most appropriate systemic drug in the absence of any contra-indications would be
explanation: Ciclosporin can induce rapid clearance as it acts quicker than most other systemic agents in psoriasis. Main side-effects/complications that require regular monitoring are renal impairment and hypertension. Prednisolone should not be used in psoriasis to avoid inducing pustular psoriasis following withdrawal.

question: A 40-year old man presented with a 6-months history of an intensely pruritic eruption which started on his limbs and genitalia. Close examination shows shiny polygonal papules with a violaceus colour; all papules were flat-topped. Examination of the mouth shows a reticular white appearance on both buccal mucosae. The diagnosis here is
explanation: The appearance of pruritic, polygonal, purple and plane papules (SPs) is characteristic of lichen planus. Oral and genital examination should always be performed when the diagnosis is suspected. Erosive lichen planus can cause scarring. Other variants of lichen plan us include: hypertrophic, atrophic, drug-induced, lichen plan us pemphigoides and lichen planus pigmentosa. 272 Section 3: Answers & Comments

question: A 20-year old patient presents with depigmented patches on the trunk and limbs. There are no associated symptoms. Which auto-immune condition is most likely to be associated with this condition?
explanation: Many auto-immune disorders can be associated with vitiligo but thyroid disease is the commonest. Measurement of thyroid antibodies should be considered in patients with vitiligo as a high titre - even in the presence of normal thyroid function tests indicates the risk for future thyroid disease.

question: A 32-year old female presented with a 4-week history of a mildly burning rash on the upper arms and torso. Examination showed erythematous annular and polycyclic plaques with scaling without scarring. She has marked photosensitivity. The presence of which antibody in this condition may be associated with a congenital heart block in the foetus?
explanation: The diagnosis is sub-acute lupus erythematosus (LE) which can present in an annular or psoriasiform pattern. Sub-acute LE can be drug induced with thlazides being the commonest implicated. Unlike discoid LE, this variant is not associated with scarring. Anti-Ro antibodies are associated with marked photosensitivity and the risk of developing congenital cardiac defects in the foetus.

question: A 60-year old man presented with a 3-month history of an eruption that consisted of flaccid pustules in the trunk and groin with background erythema. Close examination showed flaccid bullae and pustules contc1ining a fluid level giving the appearance of a hypopyon. Some pustules and bullae had ruptured forming an annular pattern of scaling. The patient had a background of lgA paraprotinaemia. What is the first-line systemic treatment for this condition in the absence of any contra-indications?
explanation: The diagnosis here is subcorneal pustular dermatosis, also called Sneddon-Wilkinson disease. The condition can be associated with myeloma or a paraprotinaemia and these should always be investigated once the diagnosis has been made. Although all the above treatments have been used, dapsone remains the most effective treatment for subcorneal pustular dermatosis. Dapsone is also very effective for dermatitis herpetiformis and bullous lupus erythematosus.

question: A 21-year old man presented with a maculo-papular eruption on the trunk with inguinal lymphadenopathy and a painless penile ulcer. History reveals that he had unprotected sexual intercourse few months before the onset of eruption. Darkfield microscopy showed the presence of treponemas. In the absence of any allergies, the first-line antibiotic in this condition is
explanation: The diagnosis in this case is secondary syphilis with primary chancre and should always be considered in the differential of a painless genital ulcer (chancre). Secondary syphilis can present as maculo-papular eruption which typically involves the palms. Other conditions that result in macular pal mar involvement are HIV-seroconversion and erythema multiforme. Penicillins are the first-line treatment in syphilis. 273 Section 3: Answers & Comments

question: A 45-year old HIV positive patient develops a widespread rash after he was commenced on co-trimoxazole. You assess the rash and carry out a SCORTEN prognostic measurement. Which of the following is not a SCORTEN parameter in the assessment of toxic epidermal necrolysls?
explanation: SCORTEN has seven parameters which also include serum urea, tachycardia and skin detachment of >10% on the first day of assessment. The higher the score, the higher the mortality risk (3-5% for one point and >90% for 6-7 points). The SCORTEN should be measured every 3 days to assess the progress / deterioration.

question: A 26-year old lady presented to the dermatologist with a 1-week history of painful tender subcutaneous nodules on the anterior aspects of both shins. Initially, tile "lumps" were very red and painful to t0uch and gradually the colour had changed to bruise-like. On examination, ankle swelling was noted. She denies other symptoms. What is the commonest cause of this condition in the U.K.?
explanation: The diagnosis is erythema nodosum, of which in the U.K. streptococcal throat infection is the commonest cause. Other causes include sarcoidosis, yersinia, hellcobacter pylori infections, actinomycosis, tuberculosis, pregnancy and the combined contraceptive pill. Measurement of anti-streptolysin titre 7-10 days following a sore throat can help confirm the streptococcal aetiology in retrospect.

question: A 68-year old lady was recently discharged from the cardiology ward following a second myocardial infarction. She presents with a 6-week history of painful ulcer in the buccal mucosa. The ulcer was oval shaped with an erythematous halo and was extremely tender to touch. She reports no other mucosa I ulceration and remains well otherwise. She is on a number of cardiac medications. Which of the following is most likely to be the cause of her oral ulceration?
explanation: Nicorandil has been increasingly linked to ulceration, both mucosa( as well as cutaneous. Recently, several reports have reported peri-stomal ulcerations and spontaneous bowel perforations. These only respond to withdrawal of the nicorandil, however healing can take several months.

question: A 3-year old boy presents to the dermatology department as his parents have concerns about several lesions on his face and trunk which he has had for over a year. Clinically, these consisted of yellow to orange coloured small nodules. There was no history of erosions, blisters, or change in size following rubbing. The child is otherwise well in himself; there is no family history of such lesions. Which would be the most appropriate next investigation?
explanation: Juvenile xanthogranuloma is a histiocytic disorder. It presents in children as solitary yellow to orange coloured lesions. Ophthalmic involvement is the most common extra-cutaneous site and should be considered in children with more than three lesions. 274 Section 3: Answers & Comments

question: A 68-year old lady was recently treated with isoniazid for prophylaxis of tuberculosis. She presented with an erythematous butterfly rash on the cheeks following sun exposure and reports arthralgia and several mouth ulcers. Her full blood count showed normocytic anaemia, and slight reduced platelet count. Her renal function is normal. Which of the following auto-antibodies will most likely be positive?
explanation: Drug-induced lupus erythematosus, should be considered in older patients with no past history of connective tissue disorders. Anti-histone antibody Is positive in the majority of patients with drug-Induced lupus (>90%}, positive ANA is also seen in these patients. Common causes of drug-induced lupus include: - Allopurlnol - Clonidine - Danazol - Hydralazine - lsoniazid - Lithium - Methyldopa - Penicillamine In the majority of the cases, drug-induced lupus tends to spare the kidneys, however, if they are involved, double stranded DNA is often positive too.

question: A 16-year old boy suffered from a sore throat for 2 weeks. Thereafter, he complained of abdominal pain, swollen ankles and a rash on the lower legs. Examination of tne rash shows multiple areas of palpable petichiae and purpura. Skin biopsy showed evidence of small vessel vasculitis with lgA deposition in the vascular walls on direct immunofluoresence. What should be the next investigation performed?
explanation: The diagnosis is Henoch-Schonlein Purpura, which is usually a self-limiting small vessel vasculitis often seen in children and young adults following a sore throat. Abdominal involvement can occur in around half of the patients. Measurement of blood pressure and urinalysis to check for renal involvement is essential. A small percentage of patients (less than 5%), may progress to chronic renal failure.

question: A 16-year old boy presented to Accident and Emergency for the third time in 1 month with a history of very painful right leg, fever (38°C), joint pains in fingers and knees and myalgia. His blood tests showed evidence of moderate renal impairment, and his father says that one of his cousins had a similar p,esentation and was treated successfully with colchicine. On examination there was a bright erythema of the leg, mimicking a cellulitis. He had marked raised C-Reactive Protein. The most likely diagnoses here is
explanation: Familial Mediterranean fever is an autosomal recessive disorder due to pyrin deficiency and presents with intermittent fever, arthritis, cellulitis-like rash on the legs, myalgia and renal impairment. Treatment with colchicine can be very effective, although more recently anti-IL 1 monoclonal antibody (anakinra) has been found to be very effective in all auto- inflammatory syndromes. Hyper lgE syndrome presents with recurrent infections with raised serum lgE levels and skin changes which are similar to atopic dermatitis. 275 Section 3: Answers & Comments

question: A 45-year old woman presents with a long history of recurrent sinusitis and ear infections. She pre.;ented a month ago to Ai:cident and Emergency with haemoptysis which was thought to be secondary to a chE:st infection. She was febrile (temperature 38.7°C) and has lost 1 stone in weight over 6 weeks. You note that she has a collapsed nasal bridge, resulting in a saddle nose appearance. Which of the following investigations is most likely to be positive?
explanation: Wegener s granulomatosis presents with recurrent sinusitis, ear involvement, and respiratory involvement with haemoptysis, arthralgia and saddle nose shape due to collapsed nasal bridge. Cutaneous involvement is found in around a third of patients, anci often consists of pair.ful small ulcers or vasculitic palpable purpura. c-ANCA is positive in around 80-90% of the patients.

question: A 10-year old girl was referred to the dermatologist with a history of sun- sensitivity resulting in small papules and vesicles, often on the face and predominantly the nose. Some of the vesicles became haemorrhagic and had healed with crusting. Examination revealed some atrophic scars on the face and the arms where the haemorrhagic vesicles were present. Provocation tests later revealed a few papules and vesicles. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Hydroa vacciniforme is a photosensitive disorder which is often diagnosed in children and tends to improve later in adult life. Typically, the lesions present with papules and vesicles, some of which may become haemorrhagic and heal with crusting and erosions. Atrophic scars can be seen as a result. Xeroderma pigmentosum (XP) is an autosomal recessive photosensitive disorder which often presents with severe photosensitivity, dryness of the skin and abnormal freckling. Patients with XP are at a greater risk of developing skin tumours at very early age. Polymorphic light eruption is a non-scarring idiopathic photosensitive disorder.

question: A 5-year old boy presented to the dermatologist with a 3-month history of progressive development of bald patches on the scalp, with pruritus and some discharging areas. On examination, there were scaly patches of alopecia with some pustules and broken hairs. Wood's light examination showed positive fluorescence. The parents report that they keep pets at home. What is the most likely organism in this case?
explanation: The history here is highly suggestive of a zoophilic dermatophyte infection of which Microsporum canis is the commonest. The commonest sources of microsporum canis are cats and dogs. Trichophyton verrucosum is also a zoophilic species; however, this is often found in cattle and infected patients develop a very inflammatory kerion- like inflammation. Trichophyton tonsurans and Trichophyton rubrum are both anthropophilic (human to human spread), and do not fluoresce under Wood s light. 276 Section 3: Answers & Comments

question: An 8-year old girl returned back from a visit to Connecticut, USA, where she was visiting her relatives. She was complaining of a slightly pruritic erythematous rash in tre lower leg, which seemed to be expanding, though on further questioning she recalls be.irig bitten by an insect whilst on a picnic. What is the most appropriate antibiotic of choice in this case?
explanation: The history and clinical examination point towards a diagnosis of erythema annulare centrifugum / Lyme s disease secondary to tick bite. These ticks are commonly found in some areas of the world. The name Lyme, relates to a town in Conn<!cticut where these cases were first reported. Although doxycycline would be the treatment of choice, this would be contra- ;ndicated in view of patient s age. Amoxicillin would be the second choice in the absence of penicillin allergy.

question: Filaggrin mutations are not associated with one of the following disorders?

choices.A: Allergic rhinitis in patients with atopic dermatitis
choices.B: Asthma in patients with atopic dermatitis

explanation: Mutations in the filaggrin gene are associated with ichthyosis vulgaris. Mutations in filaggrin are also a risk factor for atopic dermatitis and are associated with disease severity. Among patients with atopic dermatitis, mutated filaggrin is associated with asthma, allergic rhinitis and allergic sensitisation. Mutated filaggrin is not independently associated with asthma. Mutated filaggrin predicts a more severe course in alopecia areata.

question: A 35-year old lady presented with three episodes of facial swelling, more noticeable in the peri-orbital area and swelling of both hands on one occasion. The swellings were more painful than pruritic, failed to respond to anti- histamines and a short course of oral corticosteroids. Her mother had similar episodes. Laboratory investigations revealed low C4 level, with normal Cl esterase inhibitor levels, but reduced functional Cl esterase levels. Her Clq antibodies were negative. The diagnosis here is
explanation: The history and clinical findings are suggestive of the diagnosis of angio-oedema. In the absence of urticaria and the lack of response to anti-histamines, one should suspect hereditary or acquired angio-oedema. Hereditary angio-oedemas are autosomal dominant disorders. ,., The hallmark of both types 1 and 2 is reduced C4 level. In hereditary angio-oedema type 1, both C1 inhibitor levels as well as Cl functional levels are reduced. In hereditary angio-oedema type 2, Cl esterase inhibitor levels can be normal or elevated, but the functional levels are reduced. Type 3 hereditary angio-oedema is very rare. C4 and Cl esterase inhibitor levels are normal. This condition tends to be precipitated by oestrogens. A family history and absence of Clq antibodies go against the diagnosis of acquired angio-oedema. 277 Section 3: Answers & Comments

question: A 45-year old man presented with a 6-month history of multi pie crusted areas on his scalp, face and central chest. He gives a clear history of flaccid bullae that rupture easily leaving eroded areas that crust. There is no mucosal involvement. Treatment with anti-fungal creams for presumed seborrhoeic dermatitis failed to clear the lesions. Biopsy of one of the lesions showed acantholysis confined to the sub-corneal area and deposits of lgG in the epidermis on immunofluorescence. Which antigen is involved in the pathogenesis of this condition?
explanation: Pemphigus foliaceus is a milder variant of pemphigus vulgaris with flaccid bullae progressing to crusted erosions in a seborrhoeic distribution. Mucosal involvement is typically absent, and the defect is high in the epidermis in the sub-corneal layer. Desmoglein-1 can also be found in pemphigus vulgaris and pemphigus vegetans. However, in pemphigus vulgaris, Desmogleln 3 is almost always present as well. Collagen VII is the target antigen in epidermolysis bullosa acquisita. Laminin-6 is targeted in cicatricial pemphigoid. BP-180 and BP-230 are the auto-antigens targeted In bullous pemphigoid.

question: A 60-year old man developed multiple yellow plaques on the peri-orbital skin. Some of the plaques were ulcerated with a few having a te!angiectatic component. Biopsy from one of the lesions showed a palisading granuloma with necrobiosis and foamy histiocytes with giant Touton cells. The most appropriate next investigation in this patient would be
explanation: Paraproteinaemia is found in nearly three quarters of the cases of necrobiotic xanthogranuloma. This is predominantly lgG, however, lgM paraproteinaemia may also occur. Cryoglobulinaemia can also occur in about a third of the patients; therefore cryoglobulin studies should also be performed.

question: A 26-year old 34-weeks pregnant lady in her third pregnancy developed multiple urticated plaques on her thighs and abdomen with a large urticated plaque involving her umbilicus with some vesicles. She is otherwise well but is extremely concerned about her pregnancy. Which of the following statements regarding this condition is true?

choices.A: A pregnancy termination is often required
choices.B: Biopsy and lmmunofluorescence findings would be non-specific in this condition
choices.C: There is a slightly increased risk of premature labor
choices.D: This condition has no effect on the foetus and always resolves following post-partum
choices.E: This condition tends to continue many years after delivery

correct_text: There is a slightly increased risk of premature labor
explanation: Pemphigoid gestationis is a rare pregnancy-related dermatosis that often occurs in the second or third trimester. It typically presents with urticated plaques or vesicles and bullae, often with umbilical involvement. There is an increased risk for prematurity and small for gestational age babies, and less than 10% risk of the neonates have skin lesions. The condition almost always resolves post-partum, and does not tend to progress to a chronic stage. lmmunofluorescence typically shows linear C3 +/-lgG along the basement membrane zone and can be very helpful in distinguishing this condition from the urticated phase of pruritic papules and plaques of pregnancy. 278 Section 3: Answers & Comments

question: A 14-year old girl is seen in your clinic with fever and a rash. On examination of the oral mucosa, Forschheimer spots are seen. What are Forschheimer spots a feature of?
explanation: For$chheimer spots are small erythematous macules on the palate seen in Rubella (German measles). They are not a feature of congenital rubella. White Koplik spots are characteristic of measles.

question: A 26-year-old atopic patient is admitted with eczema herpeticum. Eczema herpeticum can complicate all of the following except
explanation: Eczema herpeticum is the p esence of disseminated herpes in the setting of underlying skin diseases (most commonly, atopic eczema). Besides atopic eczema, eczema herpeticum has also been associated with seborrhoeic dermatitis, Darier s disease, pemphigus vulgaris, mycosis fungoides, Wiskott-Aldrich disease, congenital ichthyosiform erythroderma, and second degree burns.

question: Which of the following is the commonest recognized cause of recurrent erythema multiforme?
explanation: Although many factors can trigger erythema multiforme, herpes simplex virus (HSV) is the commonest known trigger for this self-limiting condition. In the absence of any identifiable trigger, a long-term (6-24 months) suppressive therapy for HSV such as aciclovir 400 mg twice daily can be given for recurrent erythema multiforme.

question: A 20-year old man presents with keratotic beaded papules on the nape of the neck. Which of the following disorders is not associated with elastosis perforans serpiginosa?
explanation: Elastosis perforans serp1gmosa is a perforating disorder characterized by transepidermal elimination of elastic fibers. Hyperkeratotic pa pules varying from 2 mm to 1 cm In diameter occur in a serpiginous distribution. D-penicillamine is associated with the development of elastosis perforans serpiginosa. The neck is most commonly involved. Elastosis perforans serpiginosa is associated with Down s syndrome, acrogeria, Marfan s syndrome, Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, cutis laxa, osteogenesis imperfecta, Rothmund-Thomson syndrome and pseudoxanthoma elasticum. 279 Section 3: Answers & Comments

question: A 3-year old girl was referred by the endocrinologists with a rash on the scalp and vulva. Examination shows extensive seborrhea on the scalp with some vesicular crusted lesions and erosions on the vulva. Erosions, purpura and ulceration were also seen on the lower back. She has been diagnosed with diabetes insipidus. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Letterer-Siwe syndrome is the most severe form of Langerhan s cell histiocytosis. Usually seen in children, it is associated with exuda Cive, ulcerative seborrhoeic dermatitis-like eruption and systemic signs including hepatosplenomegaly. Suspicion of the diagnosis should arise in any child with seborrhoeic dermatitis-like picture and the presence of petechieae. Intertriginous lesions are common. Loss of teeth may occur if mandiblular and maxillary bones are involved. Lymphadenopathy, bone marrow involvement and thrombocytopaenia are also seen. Diabetes insipidus occurs secondary to involvement of the pituitary gland or hypothalamus. Triad of proptosis, diabetes insipidus and skin rash are seen In Hand-Scholler- Christian disease. The disease is commonly fulmimrnt and fatal. Vinblastine is the chemotherapeutic agent of choice.

question: A 6-month old girl is referred to the department of paediatric dermatology with a port-wine stain on the left side of her face. She is under the care of the neurologists for epilepsy. Which of the following best describes the inheritance pattern of this condition?
explanation: Sturge-Weber syndrome is a sporadic malformation of the vasculature of the leptomeninges, facial dermal capillaries and often ocular vessels. It is characterized by facial port wine stain most commonly affecting areas innervated by the ophthalmic and maxillary divisions of the trigeminal nerve. Homolateral leptomeningeal angiomatosis results in epilepsy in 75-90% of cases.

question: A 45-year old Nigerian man presents with a solitary hyperpigmented irregular macule on the palmar surface of the hand. Microscopy of skin scrapings treated with 20% KOH reveal thick, septate, branching hyphae that contain a dark pigment in their walls. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Tinea nigra is an uncommon superficial dermatomycosis usually caused by Hortaea werneckll which is classified in the family Dematiaceae. Tinea nigra appears as a hyperpigmented macule, which usually occurs on the palms. Tinea nigra is a superficial mycosis of the stratum corneum. Infection is believed to occur as a result of inoculation from a contaminated source such as soil, sewage, wood, or compost. Microscopic examination of skin scrapings treated with 20% KOH reveals thick, septate, branching hyphae that contain a dark pigment in their walls. Topical application of antifungal agents e.g. clotrimazole or ketoconazole usually lead to resolution of tin ea nigra within 2-4 weeks. 280 Section 3: Answers & Comments

question: .ti... 30-year old farmer was admitted with multiple nodules on the left leg in a sporctrichoid pattern. Gram stain of the clinical specimen showed thin, gram-positive branching filamentous bacteria, weakly positive with acid-fast staining. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Nocardiosis is caused by aerobic Gram-positive filamentous bacteria. It has a worldwide distribution, and is an environmentally acquired infection, due to primary traumatic inoculation. Pulmonary infections are mostly seen in immunocompromised patients and skin infections mostly in immunocompetent patients. Skin diseases are mostly caused by N. braslllensls and less commonly N. asteroides, N. otidiscaviarum, and N. farcinica. Cutaneous nocardiosis occurs either as cellulitis or more characteristic lymphocutaneous nodules in a sporotrichoid pattern. Skin lesions also occur in disseminated disease. Diagnosis is based on Gram stain of clinical specimen which shows thin, gram- positive branching bacteria, weakly positive with acid-fast staining. Microbiologic isolation of Nocardia sp. is diagnostic, but requires keeping cultures under observation for 5 to 7 days. Treatment of choice is sulfonamides.

question: A 25-year old Asian man is admitted with painful and tender, bright-pink, dermal and subcutaneous nodules. He is febrile and anorexic. He has been receiving anti leprosy treatment. Which of the following subtypes of leprosy was the most likely primary diagnosis?
explanation: Erythema nodosum leprosum (type II reaction) occurs most often in lepromatous leprosy (75%). It may occur before, during, or after chemotherapy. The median time of onset is almost 1 year after onset of treatment.
